docs.title: U-Boot
docs.text:
Full details: Environment presets, U-Boot commands.

setenv ipaddr 192.168.1.5
setenv serverip 192.168.1.3
setenv netmask 255.255.255.0
setenv nfsdir /nfs/rzg2l
setenv kernel Image
setenv fdtfile r9a07g044l2-smarc.dtb
setenv k_addr 0x48080000
setenv fdt_addr 0x48000000
setenv args_common 'console=ttySC0,115200n8 rootwait rw noinitrd nohlt panic=1 earlyprintk=ttySC0,115200n8'
setenv nfsboot 'setenv bootargs ${args_common} ip=${ipaddr}:${serverip}::${netmask}::eth0 root=/dev/nfs nfsroot=${serverip}:${nfsdir},nfsvers=3,tcp; tftp ${k_addr} ${kernel}; tftp ${fdt_addr} ${fdtfile}; booti ${k_addr} - ${fdt_addr}'
setenv sdboot 'setenv bootargs ${args_common} root=/dev/mmcblk1p2; mmc dev 1; ext4load mmc 1:1 ${k_addr} ${kernel}; ext4load mmc 1:1 ${fdt_addr} ${fdtfile}; booti ${k_addr} - ${fdt_addr}'
setenv emmcboot 'setenv bootargs ${args_common} root=/dev/mmcblk0p2; mmc dev 0; ext4load mmc 0:1 ${k_addr} ${kernel}; ext4load mmc 0:1 ${fdt_addr} ${fdtfile}; booti ${k_addr} - ${fdt_addr}'
setenv bootcmd 'run nfsboot'
saveenv

run sdboot                         # boot another method once
printenv bootcmd bootargs
env default -a; saveenv            # reset environment

Working with the board once it boots: console, network, peripherals from user space, kernel debugging and performance checks.

Article When to use it Serial console Connecting to the board's console from Linux, Windows or a VM Network & file transfer Static IP, SSH, scp/rsync, NFS mounts, internet through the host Peripherals from user space Testing GPIO, I2C, SPI, UART, CAN, ADC, PWM, registers from the shell Kernel debugging Probe failures, dynamic debug, oops decoding, ftrace Performance & system status CPU frequency, temperature, memory, storage speed, boot time

docs.title: Kernel debugging
docs.text:
Finding out why a driver does not probe, a device does not work, or the kernel crashes.

Most commands need CONFIG_DEBUG_FS=y and CONFIG_DYNAMIC_DEBUG=y (see Kernel config). Mount debugfs if it is not mounted already:

mount | grep -q debugfs || mount -t debugfs none /sys/kernel/debug

docs.title: Kernel log
docs.text:
dmesg -T                          # human-readable timestamps
dmesg -w                          # follow new messages
dmesg --level=err,warn            # only errors and warnings
dmesg | grep -iE "spi|1004b000"   # by driver name or register address
dmesg -C                          # clear, then reproduce the problem

docs.title: Boot arguments for debugging
docs.text:
Append to bootargs in U-Boot (see Environment presets for where bootargs is built):

Argument Effect loglevel=8 Print all messages to the console, including debug ignore_loglevel Same, regardless of later printk settings initcall_debug Log each driver init call with its duration. Shows where boot hangs or what is slow earlycon Console output before the serial driver loads, using stdout-path from the device tree. For hangs right after Starting kernel ... panic=0 Stay at the panic message instead of rebooting (panic=1 reboots after 1 s, so the message scrolls away) clk_ignore_unused Do not turn off unused clocks at boot. Tests whether a missing clock reference in the device tree causes a hang dyndbg="file drivers/spi/* +p" Enable dynamic debug messages from boot

Example, set temporarily for one boot:

setenv bootargs "${bootargs} loglevel=8 initcall_debug panic=0"
boot

docs.title: Dynamic debug
docs.text:
Turn on dev_dbg() / pr_debug() messages of one driver at runtime, without rebuilding:

echo 'file drivers/spi/spi-rspi.c +p' > /sys/kernel/debug/dynamic_debug/control
echo 'module rspi +p' > /sys/kernel/debug/dynamic_debug/control       # whole module
echo 'func rspi_probe +p' > /sys/kernel/debug/dynamic_debug/control   # one function

Turn off again with -p. See what is enabled:

grep "=p" /sys/kernel/debug/dynamic_debug/control

For a module, enable it at load time:

modprobe rspi dyndbg=+p

docs.title: Why did the driver not probe?
docs.text:
Is the device known, and is a driver bound?

ls /sys/bus/platform/devices/ | grep 1004b000
ls -l /sys/bus/platform/devices/1004b000.spi/driver

Devices waiting for a resource (clock, regulator, GPIO, PHY) that is not available yet:

cat /sys/kernel/debug/devices_deferred

Checks in order:

  1. Node status = "okay" in the live tree: cat /proc/device-tree/soc/spi@1004b000/status
  2. Driver built: zcat /proc/config.gz | grep CONFIG_SPI_RSPI
  3. Driver loaded (if module): lsmod | grep rspi
  4. Probe error in dmesg, often with an error code like -517 (-EPROBE_DEFER) or -22 (-EINVAL)

Error codes: -2 ENOENT, -12 ENOMEM, -16 EBUSY, -19 ENODEV, -22 EINVAL, -110 ETIMEDOUT, -517 EPROBE_DEFER. The full list is in include/uapi/asm-generic/errno-base.h and errno.h.

docs.title: Clocks, pins, interrupts, GPIO
docs.text:
cat /sys/kernel/debug/clk/clk_summary | grep -iE "spi|rspi"    # enable count, rate
cat /sys/kernel/debug/pinctrl/*/pinmux-pins | grep -v UNCLAIMED
cat /sys/kernel/debug/gpio
cat /proc/interrupts                                           # IRQ counts per CPU
ls /sys/kernel/debug/regmap/                                   # register dumps for regmap drivers

/proc/interrupts before and after a test shows whether the device's interrupt fires at all.

docs.title: Decode a kernel oops
docs.text:
An oops prints a call trace like rspi_transfer_one+0x48/0x1a0 [rspi]. Turn it into file and line numbers with the vmlinux (or .ko) from the same build, on the host:

cd $KSRC
./scripts/faddr2line vmlinux rspi_transfer_one+0x48/0x1a0
./scripts/faddr2line drivers/spi/spi-rspi.o rspi_transfer_one+0x48/0x1a0    # for a module

Decode a whole saved log:

./scripts/decode_stacktrace.sh vmlinux $KSRC < oops.txt

Tip

Build with CONFIG_DEBUG_INFO=y to get line numbers. Without it, only function names are available. In Yocto, vmlinux is in tmp/work/*/linux-renesas/*/build/.

docs.title: ftrace
docs.text:
Trace function calls of a driver, without adding prints:

cd /sys/kernel/debug/tracing
echo 0 > tracing_on
echo function > current_tracer
echo 'rspi_*' > set_ftrace_filter
echo 1 > tracing_on
# reproduce the problem
echo 0 > tracing_on
cat trace | head -50

Call graph with timing:

echo function_graph > current_tracer

Trace events, e.g. all SPI events or all IRQ handlers:

echo 1 > events/spi/enable
echo 1 > events/irq/irq_handler_entry/enable

Reset:

echo nop > current_tracer
echo > set_ftrace_filter
echo 0 > events/enable

Requires CONFIG_FTRACE=y, CONFIG_FUNCTION_TRACER=y, CONFIG_FUNCTION_GRAPH_TRACER=y.

docs.title: Magic SysRq
docs.text:
When the system is stuck but the console still responds (CONFIG_MAGIC_SYSRQ=y):

echo 1 > /proc/sys/kernel/sysrq
echo t > /proc/sysrq-trigger      # stack traces of all tasks
echo w > /proc/sysrq-trigger      # blocked (D state) tasks only
echo m > /proc/sysrq-trigger      # memory info
echo b > /proc/sysrq-trigger      # reboot immediately

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause / fix Nothing after Starting kernel ... Wrong dtb, wrong load address, or console not set. Add earlycon; check console=ttySC0,115200n8 Boot hangs at a random point, no message Often a clock or power domain turned off. Try clk_ignore_unused; use initcall_debug to see the last init call /sys/kernel/debug is empty debugfs not mounted (see top of page) or CONFIG_DEBUG_FS off dynamic_debug/control missing CONFIG_DYNAMIC_DEBUG off. Add #define DEBUG at the top of the driver file as a fallback faddr2line prints ?? vmlinux from a different build, or no debug info

docs.title: Network & file transfer
docs.text: Bringing up Ethernet on the board, connecting over SSH, and moving files between host and board.

docs.title: Variables
docs.text:
export BOARD_IP=192.168.1.5
export HOST_IP=192.168.1.3
export HOST_IF=enx080027effb07      # host interface connected to the board (see ip -br addr)

docs.title: Static IP on the board
docs.text:
Temporary (lost on reboot):

ip link set eth0 up
ip addr add 192.168.1.5/24 dev eth0
ip -br addr show eth0
ping -c 3 192.168.1.3

Persistent: first check which network setup the image uses:

ps -p 1 -o comm=                                   # systemd or init
ls /etc/systemd/network/ /etc/network/interfaces 2>/dev/null
systemd-networkdifupdown (/etc/network/interfaces) 
cat > /etc/systemd/network/10-eth0.network << 'EOF'
[Match]
Name=eth0

[Network]
Address=192.168.1.5/24
Gateway=192.168.1.3
DNS=8.8.8.8
EOF
systemctl restart systemd-networkd

cat >> /etc/network/interfaces << 'EOF'

auto eth0
iface eth0 inet static
    address 192.168.1.5
    netmask 255.255.255.0
    gateway 192.168.1.3
EOF
ifdown eth0; ifup eth0

Note

With NFS root, the kernel already configured eth0 from the ip= boot argument. Do not change eth0 settings then; the rootfs would disconnect.

docs.title: SSH
docs.text:
The image needs an SSH server (dropbear or openssh, e.g. IMAGE_FEATURES += "ssh-server-openssh"). With debug-tweaks, root has no password.

ssh root@$BOARD_IP

Log in without a password, using my key:

ssh-copy-id root@$BOARD_IP

Host alias in ~/.ssh/config, so ssh rz is enough. The last two lines skip the host key check: the board gets a new key every time it is reflashed.

Host rz
    HostName 192.168.1.5
    User root
    StrictHostKeyChecking no
    UserKnownHostsFile /dev/null

docs.title: Copy files
docs.text:
scp app root@$BOARD_IP:/home/root/
scp root@$BOARD_IP:/var/log/messages .
scp -r mydir root@$BOARD_IP:/home/root/

Only changed files (needs rsync on the board):

rsync -av --progress build/ root@$BOARD_IP:/home/root/build/

Run a command remotely:

ssh root@$BOARD_IP "dmesg | tail -20"

docs.title: Mount a host directory on the board (NFS)
docs.text:
When the board boots from SD/eMMC but I want quick access to host files. Export the directory on the host as in Booting with TFTP and NFS, then on the board:

mkdir -p /mnt/host
mount -t nfs -o nolock,vers=3 192.168.1.3:/nfs/share /mnt/host

docs.title: Internet access for the board through the host
docs.text:
Board connected directly to the host (no router). Share the host's internet connection with NAT.

On the host:

export WAN_IF=enp0s3       # host interface that has internet
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1
sudo iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -o $WAN_IF -j MASQUERADE
sudo iptables -A FORWARD -i $HOST_IF -o $WAN_IF -j ACCEPT
sudo iptables -A FORWARD -i $WAN_IF -o $HOST_IF -m state --state RELATED,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT

On the board:

ip route add default via 192.168.1.3
echo "nameserver 8.8.8.8" > /etc/resolv.conf
ping -c 3 google.com

docs.title: Check the link
docs.text:
ip -s link show eth0             # counters, errors
ethtool eth0                     # speed, duplex, link detected

Throughput (needs iperf3 on both sides):

iperf3 -s                        # on the host
iperf3 -c 192.168.1.3 -t 10      # on the board

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause / fix ping fails both ways Different subnets, cable on the other port (eth1), or link down: ethtool eth0 \| grep Link WARNING: REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED! Board was reflashed and has a new host key. ssh-keygen -R $BOARD_IP Connection refused on SSH No SSH server in the image, or it has not started yet. Check ps \| grep -E "sshd\|dropbear" SSH is slow to connect Board tries a reverse DNS lookup. Add UseDNS no to /etc/ssh/sshd_config on the board Board has no internet through the host Forwarding or NAT rule missing on the host, or no default route / DNS on the board Host VM cannot reach the board VirtualBox adapter must be in Bridged mode on the physical interface connected to the board

docs.title: Performance & system status
docs.text: Checking CPU, memory, temperature, storage speed and boot time on the board.

docs.title: CPU
docs.text:
nproc
lscpu
cat /proc/cpuinfo | grep -E "processor|CPU part"

Frequency and governor (cpufreq):

cat /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cpufreq/scaling_available_frequencies
cat /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_cur_freq
cat /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cpufreq/scaling_governor

Fix the CPU at maximum frequency for benchmarks (repeatable numbers):

for g in /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor; do echo performance > $g; done

docs.title: Load and processes
docs.text:
top                         # press 1 for per-CPU view, M to sort by memory
uptime
ps aux --sort=-%cpu | head

Generate CPU load for thermal or stability tests (if stress-ng is in the image):

stress-ng --cpu $(nproc) --timeout 300s --metrics-brief

Without stress-ng, one busy loop per core:

for i in $(seq $(nproc)); do (while :; do :; done) & done
# stop:
kill $(jobs -p)

docs.title: Temperature
docs.text:
for z in /sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone*; do echo "$(cat $z/type): $(( $(cat $z/temp) / 1000 )) C"; done

Watch it during a load test:

watch -n 1 'cat /sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone*/temp'

Trip points (where throttling or shutdown happens):

grep . /sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone0/trip_point_*

docs.title: Memory
docs.text:
free -h
grep -E "MemTotal|MemAvailable|Cma" /proc/meminfo

CmaTotal / CmaFree is the contiguous memory used by video, GPU and DRP-AI buffers. When multimedia fails to allocate buffers, check that CmaFree is large enough.

Largest memory users:

ps aux --sort=-rss | head

docs.title: Storage speed
docs.text:
Write and read test on the SD card or eMMC (bypasses the page cache with direct):

dd if=/dev/zero of=/home/root/test.bin bs=1M count=256 oflag=direct status=progress
dd if=/home/root/test.bin of=/dev/null bs=1M iflag=direct status=progress
rm /home/root/test.bin

Which device and filesystem the rootfs is on:

df -h /
lsblk -f

docs.title: Boot time
docs.text:
With systemd:

systemd-analyze
systemd-analyze blame | head -20
systemd-analyze critical-chain

Kernel part: timestamps in the log show when each driver finished. The time of the last kernel message before init starts is the kernel boot time:

dmesg | grep -E "Run /sbin/init|Freeing unused kernel memory"

Add initcall_debug to bootargs to see the duration of every driver init (see Kernel debugging):

dmesg | grep " returned .* after " | sed 's/.* after \([0-9]*\) usecs/\1 &/' | sort -n -r | head

docs.title: Profiling with perf
docs.text:
If the image includes perf (IMAGE_FEATURES += "tools-profile"):

perf top                                  # live, system-wide
perf stat ./app                           # counters for one run
perf record -g ./app && perf report       # where the time goes, with call graphs

docs.title: Network throughput
docs.text: See Network & file transfer (iperf3, ethtool).

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause / fix cpufreq directory missing cpufreq driver not enabled, or the SoC runs at a fixed frequency in this BSP Performance drops after a few minutes of load Thermal throttling. Check temperature and scaling_cur_freq during the test dd speeds unrealistically high Page cache used. Keep oflag=direct / iflag=direct, or sync; echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches before reading Video / GPU app fails with Cannot allocate memory while free shows plenty CMA exhausted. Check CmaFree; increase CMA in the device tree reserved-memory or with cma= boot argument

docs.title: Peripherals from user space
docs.text:
Quick tests of GPIO, I2C, SPI, UART, CAN, ADC, PWM and raw registers from the board's shell, without writing any code.

Tools needed in the image: libgpiod-tools i2c-tools spidev-test can-utils devmem2 (see BitBake commands for adding packages).

docs.title: GPIO (libgpiod)
docs.text:
gpiodetect
gpioinfo gpiochip0 | head -40

On RZ/G2L-family SoCs, the line number of port pin Pm_n is m * 8 + n (same as RZG2L_GPIO(m, n) in the device tree). Example: P43_1 → line 345.

echo $((43 * 8 + 1))
libgpiod v1 (Dunfell, Kirkstone)libgpiod v2 (Scarthgap and later) 
gpioset gpiochip0 345=1           # drive high
gpioset gpiochip0 345=0           # drive low
gpioget gpiochip0 345             # read input
gpiomon gpiochip0 345             # wait for edges (Ctrl+C to stop)

gpioset -c gpiochip0 345=1        # keeps running and holds the value; Ctrl+C to release
gpioget -c gpiochip0 345
gpiomon -c gpiochip0 345

Check the version with gpioset --version.

Note

gpioset fails with Device or resource busy if the pin is used by a driver or as a peripheral function. gpioinfo shows the consumer in the [used] column.

LEDs defined with gpio-leds in the device tree are controlled through sysfs instead:

ls /sys/class/leds/
echo 1 > /sys/class/leds/led-user/brightness
echo heartbeat > /sys/class/leds/led-user/trigger

docs.title: I2C
docs.text:
i2cdetect -l                      # list buses
i2cdetect -y 1                    # scan bus 1 (UU = address used by a kernel driver)

Read / write one register (bus 1, device 0x50, register 0x00):

i2cget -y 1 0x50 0x00
i2cset -y 1 0x50 0x00 0xab
i2cdump -y 1 0x50                 # all registers 0x00-0xff

Multi-byte transfer (write register address 0x00, then read 8 bytes):

i2ctransfer -y 1 w1@0x50 0x00 r8

Warning

For addresses shown as UU, a driver owns the device. i2cset needs -f then, and can confuse the driver. Prefer reading.

docs.title: SPI (spidev)
docs.text:
/dev/spidevX.Y exists only when a device on that bus is bound to the spidev driver:

ls /dev/spidev*

If there is none, bind one at runtime (the bus controller must be enabled in the device tree with a child node, e.g. spi1.0):

echo spidev > /sys/bus/spi/devices/spi1.0/driver_override
echo spi1.0 > /sys/bus/spi/drivers/spidev/bind

Loopback test: connect MOSI to MISO, then:

spidev_test -D /dev/spidev1.0 -s 1000000 -v -p "\x01\x02\x03\x04"

The RX line must equal the TX line. All 00 or FF means no loopback or wrong pins.

docs.title: UART
docs.text:
Ports other than the console:

ls /dev/ttySC*
stty -F /dev/ttySC1 115200 raw -echo

Loopback test (connect TX to RX):

cat /dev/ttySC1 &
echo "hello uart" > /dev/ttySC1
kill %1

Interactive (if picocom or microcom is in the image):

microcom -s 115200 /dev/ttySC1

docs.title: CAN / CAN FD
docs.text:
ip link set can0 down
ip link set can0 type can bitrate 500000
ip link set can0 up
ip -details -statistics link show can0

CAN FD (nominal 500 kbit/s, data 2 Mbit/s):

ip link set can0 type can bitrate 500000 dbitrate 2000000 fd on

Test between two channels wired together (e.g. can0 ↔ can1 with a terminated cable):

ip link set can1 type can bitrate 500000 && ip link set can1 up
candump can1 &
cansend can0 123#DEADBEEF
cansend can0 123##1.0011223344556677       # CAN FD frame
kill %1

docs.title: ADC (IIO)
docs.text:
ls /sys/bus/iio/devices/
cat /sys/bus/iio/devices/iio:device0/name
cat /sys/bus/iio/devices/iio:device0/in_voltage0_raw

docs.title: PWM
docs.text:
ls /sys/class/pwm/
echo 0 > /sys/class/pwm/pwmchip0/export
echo 1000000 > /sys/class/pwm/pwmchip0/pwm0/period         # ns -> 1 kHz
echo 500000  > /sys/class/pwm/pwmchip0/pwm0/duty_cycle     # 50 %
echo 1 > /sys/class/pwm/pwmchip0/pwm0/enable

docs.title: Raw registers (devmem)
docs.text:
Read a register directly, e.g. to check a pin function or a clock enable bit. Needs CONFIG_DEVMEM=y.

devmem2 0x11030000 w                 # read 32-bit word
devmem2 0x11030000 w 0x00000001      # write

BusyBox has an equivalent built in:

devmem 0x11030000 32

Danger

Writing a wrong register can hang the board or damage connected hardware. Read first, change one bit at a time.

Note

Reading registers of a peripheral whose clock is off returns 0 or hangs the bus. Make sure the driver is loaded (clock enabled) before reading its registers.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause / fix gpioset: error setting the GPIO line values: Device or resource busy Pin claimed by a driver or used as a peripheral function. Check gpioinfo and the pinmux in /sys/kernel/debug/pinctrl/ i2cdetect shows nothing Bus not enabled in DT, wrong bus number, missing pull-ups, or device not powered Error: Could not open file /dev/i2c-1 CONFIG_I2C_CHARDEV not enabled, or the bus is not enabled in the device tree can't open device: No such file or directory for spidev No device bound to spidev. docs.title: Serial console
docs.text: The serial console is the first thing to connect: it shows the bootloader, U-Boot, kernel log and a login shell. Settings for all RZ boards: 115200 baud, 8N1, no flow control.

docs.title: Variables
docs.text: export TTY=/dev/ttyUSB0

docs.title: Find the port
docs.text:
LinuxWindows

Plug in the board's debug USB port, then:

sudo dmesg | tail
ls -l /dev/ttyUSB* /dev/ttyACM* 2>/dev/null

usb 1-2: FTDI USB Serial Device converter now attached to ttyUSB0

Stable names that do not change when other adapters are plugged in:

ls -l /dev/serial/by-id/

Device Manager → Ports (COM & LPT) shows the port, e.g. USB Serial Port (COM5). If it shows up with a warning icon, install the USB-serial driver (FTDI / CP210x, depending on the board).

docs.title: Permissions (Linux)
docs.text:
Add my user to the dialout group once, then log out and back in:

sudo usermod -aG dialout $USER

Without this, every terminal program needs sudo.

docs.title: Connect
docs.text:
picocomminicomscreenTera Term (Windows) 
sudo apt-get install -y picocom
picocom -b 115200 $TTY

Exit: Ctrl+A then Ctrl+X.

Save everything to a log file as well:

picocom -b 115200 --logfile ~/serial-$(date +%F-%H%M).log $TTY

sudo apt-get install -y minicom
minicom -D $TTY -b 115200

Disable hardware flow control once: Ctrl+A O → Serial port setup → F → Save setup as dfl. Exit: Ctrl+A then X. Log: Ctrl+A then L.

screen $TTY 115200

Exit: Ctrl+A then K, confirm with Y.

  1. File → New connection → Serial, select the COM port.
  2. Setup → Serial port: Speed 115200, Data 8 bit, Parity none, Stop 1 bit, Flow control none.
  3. Setup → Save setup to keep the settings.

Log: File → Log.... Send a file (Flash Writer, SREC): File → Send file....

docs.title: Serial port in a VirtualBox VM
docs.text:
When the host OS is Windows and Linux runs in VirtualBox, pass the USB-serial adapter through to the VM:

  1. Power off the VM. Settings → USB: enable the USB controller and add a filter for the adapter (the + icon lists connected devices).
  2. Start the VM. The adapter disappears from Windows and appears as /dev/ttyUSB0 in Linux.

Tip

Only one side can use the port. If Tera Term on Windows is open, the VM cannot capture the device, and vice versa.

docs.title: Send a file from Linux
docs.text:
Flash Writer and the bootloader .srec/.mot files are plain text, so a raw copy to the port works (the same as Tera Term's Send file). Close the terminal program first, configure the port, then send:

stty -F $TTY 115200 cs8 -cstopb -parenb -crtscts raw
cat Flash_Writer_SCIF_RZG2L_SMARC_PMIC_DDR4_2GB_1PCS.mot > $TTY

Then reconnect with picocom to continue at the Flash Writer prompt. The full flashing procedure is in Flashing the bootloader.

docs.title: Useful on the board
docs.text:
Wider terminal after login (the serial console defaults to 80x24, so long lines wrap badly):

stty rows 50 cols 200

Kernel log level printed on the console (1 = only emergencies, 7 = everything):

echo 4 > /proc/sys/kernel/printk
dmesg -n 4

docs.text: Symptom Cause / fix Garbage characters Wrong baud rate. Use 115200 No output at all Wrong port (some boards expose two ports; try the other one), board not powered, or TX/RX swapped on a custom adapter Output works but typing does nothing Hardware flow control enabled. Disable it in the terminal settings Permission denied on /dev/ttyUSB0 Not in the dialout group (log out/in after adding), or the port is used by another program (sudo lsof $TTY) Port disappears in the VM USB filter missing or Windows program still holds the port Login prompt does not appear after kernel boot console=ttySC0,115200n8 missing in bootargs, or getty is on another tty

docs.title: Booting from SD Card and eMMC
docs.text:
Instead of loading the kernel over the network every time, Image, the device tree and the root filesystem can be stored on a micro SD card or on the on-module eMMC. U-Boot (in QSPI flash, see Flashing the bootloader) then loads them with ext4load.

Both media use the same layout:

Partition Size Filesystem Content 1 1 GB ext4 Image, r9a07g044l2-smarc.dtb 2 remaining ext4 Root filesystem

On the RZ/G2L SMARC board, Linux and U-Boot name the devices as follows:

Medium Linux device U-Boot device eMMC (on SoM) /dev/mmcblk0 mmc 0 micro SD (carrier board) /dev/mmcblk1 mmc 1

Note

The steps below are run on the board, after booting Linux with TFTP and NFS. This is the only way to write to the eMMC. Copy Image, r9a07g044l2-smarc.dtb and the rootfs tarball into the NFS rootfs (for example to /nfs/rzg2l/home/root/) so they are available on the board.

An SD card can also be prepared on a Linux host with a card reader. In that case the card shows up as /dev/sdX (check with lsblk) instead of /dev/mmcblk1.

docs.title: Create partitions
docs.text:
Danger

Partitioning erases all data on the device. Double-check the device name with lsblk before continuing.

Unmount any partitions that were mounted automatically, then open fdisk. Use /dev/mmcblk1 for the SD card or /dev/mmcblk0 for the eMMC:

umount /dev/mmcblk1p* 2>/dev/null
fdisk /dev/mmcblk1

Create partition 1 (1 GB) for the kernel and device tree:

Command (m for help): o                                # new empty DOS partition table
Command (m for help): n
Partition type
   p   primary (0 primary, 0 extended, 4 free)
   e   extended (container for logical partitions)
Select (default p): <Enter>
Partition number (1-4, default 1): <Enter>
First sector (2048-62333951, default 2048): <Enter>
Last sector, +/-sectors or +/-size{K,M,G,T,P} (...): +1G

Create partition 2 using the remaining space for the root filesystem:

Command (m for help): n
Select (default p): <Enter>
Partition number (2-4, default 2): <Enter>
First sector (...): <Enter>
Last sector, +/-sectors or +/-size{K,M,G,T,P} (...): <Enter>

Write the partition table and exit:

Command (m for help): w

docs.title: Format partitions
docs.text:
mkfs.ext4 -L boot   /dev/mmcblk1p1
mkfs.ext4 -L rootfs /dev/mmcblk1p2

docs.title: Copy kernel, device tree and rootfs
docs.text:
Copy Image and the device tree to partition 1:

mount /dev/mmcblk1p1 /mnt
cp ~/Image ~/r9a07g044l2-smarc.dtb /mnt/
sync
umount /mnt

Extract the root filesystem to partition 2:

mount /dev/mmcblk1p2 /mnt
tar -xf ~/<rootfs>.tar.bz2 -C /mnt
sync
umount /mnt

Tip

Extract the tarball directly into the mount point with tar -C rather than copying the archive onto the partition first. This avoids leaving a large .tar.bz2 file in the root filesystem.

docs.title: U-Boot config
docs.text:
Power on the board and press any key to stop autoboot.

SD cardeMMC 
setenv bootcmd 'mmc dev 1; ext4load mmc 1:1 0x48080000 Image; ext4load mmc 1:1 0x48000000 r9a07g044l2-smarc.dtb; booti 0x48080000 - 0x48000000'
setenv bootargs 'console=ttySC0,115200n8 rootwait root=/dev/mmcblk1p2 rw noinitrd nohlt panic=1 earlyprintk=ttySC0,115200n8'

setenv bootcmd 'mmc dev 0; ext4load mmc 0:1 0x48080000 Image; ext4load mmc 0:1 0x48000000 r9a07g044l2-smarc.dtb; booti 0x48080000 - 0x48000000'
setenv bootargs 'console=ttySC0,115200n8 rootwait root=/dev/mmcblk0p2 rw noinitrd nohlt panic=1 earlyprintk=ttySC0,115200n8'

What the commands do:

  • mmc dev <n>: select the MMC device (0 = eMMC, 1 = SD card).
  • ext4load mmc <dev>:<part> <addr> <file>: load a file from an ext4 partition into RAM. The kernel goes to 0x48080000 and the device tree to 0x48000000, the same addresses as in the TFTP setup.
  • booti <kernel> - <fdt>: boot an arm64 Image. The - means there is no initramfs.
  • root=/dev/mmcblkXp2 rootwait: mount partition 2 as rootfs, and wait until the MMC device is ready.

Warning

The file names in ext4load must match the files on partition 1 exactly. If you stored them under other names (for example Image_scif), update bootcmd accordingly.

Before saving, you can check that U-Boot sees the files:

mmc dev 1
ext4ls mmc 1:1

Save the environment so the board boots this way automatically (optional), then boot:

saveenv
boot

docs.title: Network access after boot (optional)
docs.text:
Unlike NFS boot, the kernel does not configure Ethernet when booting from SD/eMMC. To reach the board from the host (for ssh, scp, ...), bring up eth0 with a static IP on the same subnet as the host:

ip link set eth0 up
ip addr add 192.168.1.5/24 dev eth0
ip addr show eth0
ping 192.168.1.3      # host IP

The host can then connect with ssh root@192.168.1.5. This setting is lost on reboot.

docs.title: Other boards
docs.text:
The same procedure works on other RZ boards. Only the device tree name (and the MMC device numbers) change:

Board Device tree RZ/G2L SMARC EVK r9a07g044l2-smarc.dtb RZ/V2N EVK r9a09g056n48-rzv2n-evk.dtb RZ/G3E SMARC EVK r9a09g047e57-smarc.dtb

docs.title: Flashing a full SD card image
docs.text: The fastest way to get a bootable SD card: write the .wic image produced by Yocto. It already contains the partition table, kernel, device tree and root filesystem. Compared to building the partitions by hand, there is nothing to partition or copy.

docs.title: Variables
docs.text:
export DEPLOY=~/yocto/rzg2l_vlp_v3.0.x/build/tmp/deploy/images/smarc-rzg2l
export WIC=$DEPLOY/core-image-minimal-smarc-rzg2l.wic.gz
export SDCARD=/dev/sdX          # set after checking lsblk

docs.title: Find the SD card device
docs.text:
lsblk -d -o NAME,SIZE,MODEL,TRAN

Insert the card, run it again, and take the new entry (sdb, sdc, or mmcblk0 for a built-in reader).

Danger

Writing to the wrong device destroys its data (possibly the host's own disk). The SD card is the device that appears only after inserting the card, with the card's size.

docs.title: Write the image
docs.text:
Linux: bmaptool (fast)Linux: ddWindows

Writes only the used blocks, using the .wic.bmap file next to the image:

sudo umount ${SDCARD}* 2>/dev/null
sudo bmaptool copy $WIC $SDCARD

sudo umount ${SDCARD}* 2>/dev/null
gunzip -c $WIC | sudo dd of=$SDCARD bs=4M conv=fsync status=progress

For .wic.xz use xz -dc, for .wic.bz2 use bzip2 -dc.

  1. Decompress the .wic.gz (7-Zip) to get the .wic file.
  2. Write it with balenaEtcher or Win32 Disk Imager (rename to .img if the tool does not list .wic).
  3. Ignore the Windows message asking to format the disk. Click Cancel.

docs.title: Check the partitions
docs.text:
sudo fdisk -l $SDCARD
lsblk $SDCARD

Mount and look at the content, to know where the kernel and dtb are:

sudo mount ${SDCARD}1 /mnt && ls /mnt && sudo umount /mnt
sudo mount ${SDCARD}2 /mnt && ls /mnt /mnt/boot && sudo umount /mnt

docs.title: Boot from the card
docs.text:
Insert the card into the board and stop at the U-Boot prompt. Check where the files are from U-Boot as well:

mmc dev 1
mmc part
ls mmc 1:1
ls mmc 1:2 /boot

If the BSP's default environment already boots from SD, boot is enough. Otherwise set bootcmd according to where Image was found:

Kernel on partition 1Kernel in /boot of partition 2 
setenv bootargs 'console=ttySC0,115200n8 rootwait root=/dev/mmcblk1p2 rw'
setenv bootcmd 'mmc dev 1; load mmc 1:1 0x48080000 Image; load mmc 1:1 0x48000000 r9a07g044l2-smarc.dtb; booti 0x48080000 - 0x48000000'
saveenv
boot

setenv bootargs 'console=ttySC0,115200n8 rootwait root=/dev/mmcblk1p2 rw'
setenv bootcmd 'mmc dev 1; load mmc 1:2 0x48080000 /boot/Image; load mmc 1:2 0x48000000 /boot/r9a07g044l2-smarc.dtb; booti 0x48080000 - 0x48000000'
saveenv
boot

docs.title: Grow the rootfs to the full card
docs.text:
The .wic rootfs partition is only as big as the image. Extend it to use the whole card, on the host with the card inserted (not mounted):

sudo parted $SDCARD resizepart 2 100%
sudo e2fsck -f ${SDCARD}2
sudo resize2fs ${SDCARD}2

Note

For a built-in reader the partitions are named ${SDCARD}p1, ${SDCARD}p2 (for example /dev/mmcblk0p2).

docs.title: Write the same image to eMMC
docs.text:
The eMMC is only reachable from the board. Boot Linux from SD or NFS, copy the .wic.gz and .wic.bmap to the board, then:

bmaptool copy core-image-minimal-smarc-rzg2l.wic.gz /dev/mmcblk0

Or without bmaptool:

gunzip -c core-image-minimal-smarc-rzg2l.wic.gz | dd of=/dev/mmcblk0 bs=4M conv=fsync

Then use mmc 0 and root=/dev/mmcblk0p2 in the U-Boot commands above.

Warning

Do not write to /dev/mmcblk0 while the board's root filesystem is on it. Boot from SD or NFS first.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause / fix bmaptool: ERROR: cannot open bmap file .wic.bmap missing next to the image. Use bmaptool copy --nobmap or dd dd: failed to open '/dev/sdX': Permission denied Run with sudo, and check SDCARD is set to the real device Board does not find the card in U-Boot Card not fully inserted, or SW settings select eMMC for SDHI0. mmc rescan, mmc list Kernel boots but Waiting for root device /dev/mmcblk1p2... forever Wrong root= (SD vs. eMMC number), or the card's rootfs partition has a different number. Check mmc part resize2fs: Bad magic number in super-block Wrong partition. Check with lsblk -f which partition is ext4

docs.text:
Working with the RZ Linux kernel directly: building outside Yocto, fast test loops, configuration, device tree, modules and patches.

docs.title: Build the kernel
docs.text: Building the kernel from a git tree, outside Yocto. Much faster than bitbake for edit–build–test cycles.

docs.title: Variables
docs.text:
export KSRC=~/work/rz_linux-cip                 # kernel tree
export BSP_DIR=~/yocto/rzg2l_vlp_v3.0.x         # Yocto BSP (to read the recipe / .config)
export SDK_DIR=/opt/poky/3.1.x                  # installed Yocto SDK
export DTB=renesas/r9a07g044l2-smarc.dtb        # see table below
export JOBS=$(nproc)
Board DTB RZ/G2L SMARC EVK renesas/r9a07g044l2-smarc.dtb RZ/G3S SMARC EVK renesas/r9a08g045s33-smarc.dtb RZ/G3E SMARC EVK renesas/r9a09g047e57-smarc.dtb RZ/V2N EVK renesas/r9a09g056n48-rzv2n-evk.dtb

docs.title: Get the same source as Yocto
docs.text:
The BSP kernel lives in renesas-rz/rz_linux-cip. To work on exactly the version the BSP builds, read the branch and commit from the recipe:

cd $BSP_DIR && source poky/oe-init-build-env build
bitbake -e linux-renesas | grep -E "^(KBRANCH|SRCREV|SRC_URI)="

Clone and check out that commit:

git clone https://github.com/renesas-rz/rz_linux-cip.git $KSRC
cd $KSRC
git checkout -b work <SRCREV>

Note

Patches added by .bbappend files in meta-renesas or my layer are not in this tree. Apply them with git am if I need them (see bitbake-layers show-appends | grep linux-renesas).

docs.title: Set up the toolchain
docs.text:
Yocto SDK (recommended)Ubuntu cross compiler 
source $SDK_DIR/environment-setup-aarch64-poky-linux
unset LDFLAGS

The SDK sets ARCH=arm64 and CROSS_COMPILE=aarch64-poky-linux-. unset LDFLAGS is required: the SDK's value is meant for gcc and breaks the kernel link.

sudo apt-get install -y gcc-aarch64-linux-gnu bison flex libssl-dev bc
export ARCH=arm64
export CROSS_COMPILE=aarch64-linux-gnu-

docs.title: Configure
docs.text:
Option 1: the default config of the tree:

cd $KSRC
make defconfig

Option 2: the exact config Yocto used (best when replacing the kernel of an existing image):

cp $BSP_DIR/build/tmp/work/*/linux-renesas/*/build/.config $KSRC/.config
make olddefconfig

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
Everything (kernel, all device trees, modules):

make -j$JOBS Image dtbs modules

Only the kernel, or only one device tree:

make -j$JOBS Image
make $DTB

Output:

File Path Kernel arch/arm64/boot/Image Device tree arch/arm64/boot/dts/$DTB Kernel release string make -s kernelrelease

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Kernel and dtb to the TFTP server (see Booting with TFTP and NFS):

sudo cp arch/arm64/boot/Image arch/arm64/boot/dts/$DTB /srv/tftp/

Modules: install into a staging directory, then copy into the rootfs. sudo make would lose the cross-compile environment, so stage as a normal user first:

rm -rf /tmp/mod && make modules_install INSTALL_MOD_PATH=/tmp/mod INSTALL_MOD_STRIP=1
sudo cp -r /tmp/mod/lib/modules/* /nfs/rzg2l/lib/modules/

Check on the board that the running kernel and the modules match:

uname -r
ls /lib/modules/

docs.title: Out-of-tree build directory
docs.text:
Keep the source clean and build several configs from one tree with O=:

make O=~/work/build-g2l defconfig
make O=~/work/build-g2l -j$JOBS Image dtbs modules

All output paths above are then relative to ~/work/build-g2l.

docs.text: Symptom Cause / fix aarch64-poky-linux-ld: unrecognized option '-Wl,-O1' Run unset LDFLAGS after sourcing the SDK make: aarch64-poky-linux-gcc: No such file or directory SDK environment not sourced in this shell Board boots but modprobe fails with Exec format error / invalid module format Modules built from a different config or version than the running Image. Install both from the same build uname -r ends with + or -dirty Tree has uncommitted changes. Harmless, but /lib/modules/<release> must match it exactly Kernel hangs right after Starting kernel ... Wrong dtb for the board, or console= missing in bootargs. Check the dtb name first

docs.title: Kernel config
docs.text: Finding, changing and keeping kernel configuration options.

docs.title: Variables
docs.text:
export KSRC=~/work/rz_linux-cip
export SDK_DIR=/opt/poky/3.1.x

source $SDK_DIR/environment-setup-aarch64-poky-linux && unset LDFLAGS
cd $KSRC

docs.title: Interactive: menuconfig
docs.text:
sudo apt-get install -y libncurses-dev     # once
make menuconfig

Inside menuconfig:

Key Action / Search for a symbol (without CONFIG_), shows location and dependencies 1, 2, ... In search results: jump to that entry y / m / n Built-in / module / disabled ? Help for the selected option, including Depends on: and Selected by:

docs.title: Scripted: scripts/config
docs.text:
Faster than menuconfig when I already know the symbol names, and easy to copy:

scripts/config --enable  CONFIG_SPI_SPIDEV
scripts/config --module  CONFIG_CAN_RCAR_CANFD
scripts/config --disable CONFIG_DEBUG_INFO
scripts/config --set-val CONFIG_LOG_BUF_SHIFT 18
scripts/config --set-str CONFIG_LOCALVERSION "-mytest"
make olddefconfig          # resolve dependencies after editing

Check the result:

grep -E "SPIDEV|CANFD|LOCALVERSION=" .config

Warning

scripts/config writes the value even if dependencies are not met; make olddefconfig may then silently turn it off again. Always grep .config after olddefconfig.

docs.title: Which option builds a driver?
docs.text:
From a source file name to its config symbol:

grep -rn "sh-sci.o" drivers/tty/serial/Makefile

obj-$(CONFIG_SERIAL_SH_SCI) += sh-sci.o

From a device tree compatible string to the driver:

grep -rln '"renesas,scif-r9a07g044"' drivers/

docs.title: Save and compare configs
docs.text:
Minimal defconfig (only the non-default values):

make savedefconfig
cp defconfig arch/arm64/configs/my_defconfig
make my_defconfig          # later: load it again

Compare two configs:

scripts/diffconfig .config.old .config

 SPI_SPIDEV n -> y
+CAN_RCAR_CANFD m

docs.title: Config fragments
docs.text:
A fragment is a small file with only the options I change. Merge it on top of a base config:

cat > ~/work/my-debug.cfg << 'EOF'
CONFIG_IKCONFIG=y
CONFIG_IKCONFIG_PROC=y
CONFIG_DEBUG_FS=y
CONFIG_DYNAMIC_DEBUG=y
EOF

scripts/kconfig/merge_config.sh -m .config ~/work/my-debug.cfg
make olddefconfig

The same .cfg file goes into Yocto through a .bbappend (see Custom layer & bbappend).

docs.title: Read the config on the board
docs.text:
Requires CONFIG_IKCONFIG_PROC=y:

zcat /proc/config.gz | grep -E "SPIDEV|CANFD"

Without it, check the module directory instead:

ls /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/kernel/drivers/spi/

docs.title: Options I usually enable for development
docs.text:
# read the running config from /proc/config.gz
CONFIG_IKCONFIG=y
CONFIG_IKCONFIG_PROC=y
# debugfs: pinctrl, clk, regmap, gpio info under /sys/kernel/debug

CONFIG_SPI_SPIDEV=y

CONFIG_KALLSYMS=y

Search it in menuconfig (/) and enable what Depends on: lists Option not shown in menuconfig Its depends on is false, or wrong ARCH. Make sure ARCH=arm64 is set /proc/config.gz missing CONFIG_IKCONFIG_PROC not set in the running kernel Yocto ignores my changes made with make menuconfig in the work dir They are lost on rebuild. docs.title: Device tree
docs.text: Reading, modifying and debugging the device tree of RZ boards.

docs.title: Variables
docs.text:
export KSRC=~/work/rz_linux-cip
export DTS_DIR=$KSRC/arch/arm64/boot/dts/renesas
export BOARD_DTS=r9a07g044l2-smarc        # without extension

docs.title: File structure
docs.text:
A board .dts is built from several include files: SoC → SoM → carrier board. List what a board includes:

grep -n "#include" $DTS_DIR/$BOARD_DTS.dts

Typical layering for RZ SMARC boards:

Level RZ/G2L example Content SoC family r9a07g044.dtsi All on-chip peripherals, disabled by default SoC variant r9a07g044l2.dtsi CPU count / package-specific parts SoM rzg2l-smarc-som.dtsi Parts on the module: DDR, PMIC, eMMC, Ethernet PHY Carrier rzg2l-smarc.dtsi Connectors on the carrier board: SD slot, audio, CAN, PMOD Board r9a07g044l2-smarc.dts Top level, ties everything together

The RZ/G3S file list is in the RZ/G3S page.

Tip

Do not search through all the includes by hand. Build the dtb and decompile it to see the final merged tree (next section).

docs.title: See the final tree
docs.text:
Build and decompile:

make renesas/$BOARD_DTS.dtb
dtc -I dtb -O dts -o /tmp/$BOARD_DTS.dts $DTS_DIR/$BOARD_DTS.dtb 2>/dev/null
less /tmp/$BOARD_DTS.dts

The preprocessed source (all #include and macros expanded, labels kept) is also left in the build tree:

less $DTS_DIR/.$BOARD_DTS.dtb.dts.tmp

docs.title: Common modifications
docs.text: Put board changes in the board .dts (or my own .dts that includes it), and refer to existing nodes by label with &label. Do not edit the SoC .dtsi.

docs.title: Enable a peripheral
docs.text:
&spi1 {
    pinctrl-0 = <&spi1_pins>;
    pinctrl-names = "default";
    status = "okay";
};

docs.title: Disable a peripheral
docs.text:
&canfd {
    status = "disabled";
};

docs.title: Pin multiplexing (RZ/G2L family)
docs.text:
Pin functions are set with RZG2L_PORT_PINMUX(port, pin, function) from include/dt-bindings/pinctrl/rzg2l-pinctrl.h. Port, pin and function number come from the pin function table in the SoC hardware manual.

#include <dt-bindings/pinctrl/rzg2l-pinctrl.h>

&pinctrl {
    spi1_pins: spi1 {
        pinmux = <RZG2L_PORT_PINMUX(<port>, <pin>, <func>)>,   /* CK */
                 <RZG2L_PORT_PINMUX(<port>, <pin>, <func>)>,   /* MOSI */
                 <RZG2L_PORT_PINMUX(<port>, <pin>, <func>)>,   /* MISO */
                 <RZG2L_PORT_PINMUX(<port>, <pin>, <func>)>;   /* SSL */
    };
};

Warning

Many carrier-board pins are shared between functions (selected by DIP switches on the SMARC carrier). Check the board schematic and the switch settings before assigning a pin.

docs.title: GPIO: LED and button
docs.text:
#include <dt-bindings/gpio/gpio.h>
#include <dt-bindings/input/input.h>

/ {
    leds {
        compatible = "gpio-leds";
        led-user {
            gpios = <&pinctrl RZG2L_GPIO(<port>, <pin>) GPIO_ACTIVE_HIGH>;
            linux,default-trigger = "heartbeat";
        };
    };

    keys {
        compatible = "gpio-keys";
        key-user {
            gpios = <&pinctrl RZG2L_GPIO(<port>, <pin>) GPIO_ACTIVE_LOW>;
            linux,code = <KEY_ENTER>;
            label = "user-key";
        };
    };
};

docs.title: I2C device
docs.text:
&i2c1 {
    status = "okay";

    eeprom@50 {
        compatible = "atmel,24c02";
        reg = <0x50>;
    };
};

docs.title: Remove nodes or properties
docs.text:
&i2c1 {
    /delete-node/ codec@1a;
};

&sdhi1 {
    /delete-property/ cd-gpios;
};

docs.title: Inspect the live tree on the board
docs.text:
The running tree is exposed under /proc/device-tree (a link to /sys/firmware/devicetree/base):

cat /proc/device-tree/model; echo
ls /proc/device-tree/soc/

Check a node's status and properties:

cat /proc/device-tree/soc/spi@1004b000/status; echo
hexdump -C /proc/device-tree/soc/spi@1004b000/reg

Dump the whole live tree as source (if dtc is installed on the board):

dtc -I fs -O dts /proc/device-tree 2>/dev/null | less

docs.title: Is the driver bound?
docs.text:
ls /sys/bus/platform/devices/ | grep spi
ls -l /sys/bus/platform/devices/1004b000.spi/driver

A missing driver link means no driver was bound. Check:

dmesg | grep -i 1004b000
cat /sys/kernel/debug/devices_deferred      # probe waiting for a resource (clock, GPIO, regulator)

Pin mux state (requires CONFIG_DEBUG_FS):

cat /sys/kernel/debug/pinctrl/*/pinmux-pins | grep -v UNCLAIMED

docs.title: Validate against bindings
docs.text:
Bindings (the rules each node must follow) are in Documentation/devicetree/bindings/. Find the binding for a compatible:

grep -rl "renesas,rspi" $KSRC/Documentation/devicetree/bindings/

Check a dtb against the schemas:

pip3 install --user dtschema
make dtbs_check DT_SCHEMA_FILES=spi/renesas,rspi.yaml

docs.title: Device tree overlays in U-Boot
docs.text:
Apply a small .dtbo on top of the base dtb at boot, without rebuilding the base dtb. The base dtb must be built with symbols (DTC_FLAGS=-@).

Overlay source my-overlay.dtso:

/dts-v1/;
/plugin/;

&spi1 {
    status = "okay";
};

Build:

make DTC_FLAGS=-@ renesas/$BOARD_DTS.dtb
dtc -@ -I dts -O dtb -o my-overlay.dtbo my-overlay.dtso

In U-Boot (example with TFTP):

tftp 0x48000000 r9a07g044l2-smarc.dtb
fdt addr 0x48000000
fdt resize 8192
tftp 0x48010000 my-overlay.dtbo
fdt apply 0x48010000
tftp 0x48080000 Image
booti 0x48080000 - 0x48000000

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause / fix Error: ... syntax error with a line number in .dtb.dts.tmp Look up that line in the preprocessed file, not the original .dts Reference to non-existent node or label "xxx" Label defined in a file not included, or misspelled. Search with grep -rn "xxx:" $DTS_DIR Node is okay but device missing in Linux Driver not enabled in the kernel config, or probe deferred. Check devices_deferred and dmesg pin ... already requested by ... in dmesg Two nodes claim the same pin. Disable the other user or change the pinmux fdt apply fails with FDT_ERR_NOTFOUND Base dtb built without -@, so labels are not available to the overlay

docs.title: Fast edit–test loop
docs.text:
The loop I use when changing the kernel or device tree: build on the host, copy to TFTP/NFS, reboot the board. No SD card swapping, no BitBake. One iteration takes well under a minute for a device tree change.

Prerequisites:

  • Board boots with TFTP + NFS (Booting with TFTP and NFS), with saveenv done so it autoboots that way.
  • Kernel tree and toolchain set up (Build the kernel).

docs.title: Variables
docs.text:
export KSRC=~/work/rz_linux-cip
export SDK_DIR=/opt/poky/3.1.x
export DTB=renesas/r9a07g044l2-smarc.dtb
export TFTP_DIR=/srv/tftp
export NFS_ROOT=/nfs/rzg2l
export BOARD_IP=192.168.1.5

docs.title: Deploy script
docs.text:
Save as ~/bin/kdeploy and chmod +x ~/bin/kdeploy. It builds what is needed and copies the results to TFTP/NFS.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# usage: kdeploy [all|kernel|dtb|modules]   (default: all)
set -euo pipefail

: "${KSRC:?set KSRC}" "${SDK_DIR:?set SDK_DIR}" "${DTB:?set DTB}"
TFTP_DIR=${TFTP_DIR:-/srv/tftp}
NFS_ROOT=${NFS_ROOT:-/nfs/rzg2l}
what=${1:-all}

source "$SDK_DIR"/environment-setup-aarch64-poky-linux
unset LDFLAGS
cd "$KSRC"

if [[ $what == all || $what == kernel ]]; then
    make -j"$(nproc)" Image
    sudo cp arch/arm64/boot/Image "$TFTP_DIR"/
fi

if [[ $what == all || $what == dtb ]]; then
    make "$DTB"
    sudo cp arch/arm64/boot/dts/"$DTB" "$TFTP_DIR"/
fi

if [[ $what == all || $what == modules ]]; then
    make -j"$(nproc)" modules
    rm -rf /tmp/kmod
    make modules_install INSTALL_MOD_PATH=/tmp/kmod INSTALL_MOD_STRIP=1
    sudo rm -rf "$NFS_ROOT"/lib/modules/"$(make -s kernelrelease)"
    sudo cp -r /tmp/kmod/lib/modules/* "$NFS_ROOT"/lib/modules/
fi

echo "Deployed ($what): $(make -s kernelrelease)"

docs.title: Use it
docs.text:
Device tree change only:

kdeploy dtb

Driver change built into the kernel:

kdeploy kernel

Then reboot the board (from its serial console or over SSH):

ssh root@$BOARD_IP reboot

U-Boot loads the new files from TFTP automatically.

docs.title: Faster: reload a module without rebooting
docs.text:
When the driver is built as a module (=m), there is no need to reboot. The NFS rootfs already has the new .ko after kdeploy modules:

ssh root@$BOARD_IP "rmmod my_driver; modprobe my_driver; dmesg | tail -20"

docs.title: Check the board runs the new build
docs.text:
Each build increments the build number in uname -v (#2, #3, ...) and updates the build time:

ssh root@$BOARD_IP uname -v

#7 SMP PREEMPT Fri Oct 17 10:12:44 +07 2026

For device tree changes, read the property back from the live tree:

ssh root@$BOARD_IP "cat /proc/device-tree/model; echo"

docs.title: Speed up rebuilds with ccache
docs.text:
sudo apt-get install -y ccache
make -j$(nproc) CROSS_COMPILE="ccache aarch64-poky-linux-" Image
ccache -s          # hit statistics

Most useful after make clean, switching branches, or rebuilding the same commit in several trees.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause / fix Board boots the old kernel U-Boot env not saved for TFTP boot (printenv bootcmd), or files copied to another directory than the TFTP server root TFTP error: 'File not found' File name in bootcmd differs from the copied file. The DTB is copied without the renesas/ prefix Board hangs at NFS mount after reboot Host IP changed or NFS server stopped. Check showmount -e on the host modprobe: FATAL: Module not found uname -r on the board differs from the installed modules directory. Run kdeploy all so kernel and modules match

docs.title: Kernel module
docs.text: Templates for out-of-tree kernel modules: a minimal module, a platform driver bound from the device tree, and how to build them with a kernel tree, the SDK, or Yocto.

docs.title: Variables
docs.text:
export KDIR=~/work/rz_linux-cip       # a configured and built kernel tree
export SDK_DIR=/opt/poky/3.1.x
export BOARD_IP=192.168.1.5

Warning

The module must be built against the same kernel (version and config) that runs on the board, otherwise loading fails with invalid module format.

docs.title: Minimal module
docs.text:
hello.c:

// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0
#include <linux/module.h>
#include <linux/init.h>

static int count = 1;
module_param(count, int, 0644);
MODULE_PARM_DESC(count, "Number of greetings");

static int __init hello_init(void)
{
	int i;

	for (i = 0; i < count; i++)
		pr_info("hello: init %d\n", i);
	return 0;
}

static void __exit hello_exit(void)
{
	pr_info("hello: exit\n");
}

module_init(hello_init);
module_exit(hello_exit);

MODULE_LICENSE("GPL");
MODULE_AUTHOR("Nhat Tran");
MODULE_DESCRIPTION("Hello world module");

Makefile (works for all build methods below):

obj-m := hello.o

KDIR ?= /lib/modules/$(shell uname -r)/build
PWD  := $(shell pwd)

all:
	$(MAKE) -C $(KDIR) M=$(PWD) modules

modules_install:
	$(MAKE) -C $(KDIR) M=$(PWD) modules_install

clean:
	$(MAKE) -C $(KDIR) M=$(PWD) clean

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
Against my kernel treeAgainst the SDK kernel source 
source $SDK_DIR/environment-setup-aarch64-poky-linux && unset LDFLAGS
make KDIR=$KDIR

Requires kernel-devsrc in the SDK (see SDK). Prepare the kernel source once:

source $SDK_DIR/environment-setup-aarch64-poky-linux && unset LDFLAGS
cd $SDKTARGETSYSROOT/usr/src/kernel
sudo -E make scripts prepare
cd -

Then build the module:

make KDIR=$SDKTARGETSYSROOT/usr/src/kernel

Check the result:

modinfo hello.ko

vermagic:       5.10.xxx-cip-yocto-standard SMP preempt mod_unload aarch64

vermagic must match uname -r on the board.

docs.title: Load on the board
docs.text:
scp hello.ko root@$BOARD_IP:/home/root/

On the board:

insmod hello.ko count=3
dmesg | tail
cat /sys/module/hello/parameters/count
rmmod hello

Install it so modprobe can find it (and load dependencies automatically):

mkdir -p /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/extra
cp hello.ko /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/extra/
depmod -a
modprobe hello

Load at boot (systemd):

echo hello > /etc/modules-load.d/hello.conf

docs.title: Platform driver template
docs.text:
A driver probed from a device tree node. Covers the parts I need most often: matching, register mapping, clock, IRQ, and a sysfs attribute.

mydrv.c:

// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0
#include <linux/clk.h>
#include <linux/interrupt.h>
#include <linux/io.h>
#include <linux/module.h>
#include <linux/of.h>
#include <linux/platform_device.h>

struct mydrv {
	struct device *dev;
	void __iomem *base;
	struct clk *clk;
	int irq;
};

static irqreturn_t mydrv_irq(int irq, void *data)
{
	struct mydrv *priv = data;

	dev_dbg(priv->dev, "irq\n");
	return IRQ_HANDLED;
}

static ssize_t reg0_show(struct device *dev, struct device_attribute *attr,
			 char *buf)
{
	struct mydrv *priv = dev_get_drvdata(dev);

	return sprintf(buf, "0x%08x\n", readl(priv->base));
}
static DEVICE_ATTR_RO(reg0);

static int mydrv_probe(struct platform_device *pdev)
{
	struct device *dev = &pdev->dev;
	struct mydrv *priv;
	int ret;

	priv = devm_kzalloc(dev, sizeof(*priv), GFP_KERNEL);
	if (!priv)
		return -ENOMEM;
	priv->dev = dev;

	priv->base = devm_platform_ioremap_resource(pdev, 0);
	if (IS_ERR(priv->base))
		return PTR_ERR(priv->base);

	priv->clk = devm_clk_get(dev, NULL);
	if (IS_ERR(priv->clk))
		return dev_err_probe(dev, PTR_ERR(priv->clk), "no clock\n");
	ret = clk_prepare_enable(priv->clk);
	if (ret)
		return ret;

	priv->irq = platform_get_irq(pdev, 0);
	if (priv->irq < 0) {
		ret = priv->irq;
		goto err_clk;
	}
	ret = devm_request_irq(dev, priv->irq, mydrv_irq, 0, dev_name(dev), priv);
	if (ret)
		goto err_clk;

	platform_set_drvdata(pdev, priv);

	ret = device_create_file(dev, &dev_attr_reg0);
	if (ret)
		goto err_clk;

	dev_info(dev, "probed, irq %d\n", priv->irq);
	return 0;

err_clk:
	clk_disable_unprepare(priv->clk);
	return ret;
}

static int mydrv_remove(struct platform_device *pdev)
{
	struct mydrv *priv = platform_get_drvdata(pdev);

	device_remove_file(&pdev->dev, &dev_attr_reg0);
	clk_disable_unprepare(priv->clk);
	return 0;
}

static const struct of_device_id mydrv_of_match[] = {
	{ .compatible = "mycompany,mydrv" },
	{ /* sentinel */ }
};
MODULE_DEVICE_TABLE(of, mydrv_of_match);

static struct platform_driver mydrv_driver = {
	.probe = mydrv_probe,
	.remove = mydrv_remove,
	.driver = {
		.name = "mydrv",
		.of_match_table = mydrv_of_match,
	},
};
module_platform_driver(mydrv_driver);

MODULE_LICENSE("GPL");
MODULE_DESCRIPTION("Platform driver template");

Note

.remove returns int in 5.10 and 6.1 kernels. From 6.11 on, platform drivers use .remove returning void (temporarily .remove_new in 6.3–6.10). Adjust to the kernel version.

Matching device tree node (see Device tree). The address, IRQ, clock and reset values here are placeholders: take them from the hardware manual or from the SoC .dtsi node of the peripheral.

/ {
    mydrv@10049c00 {
        compatible = "mycompany,mydrv";
        reg = <0 0x10049c00 0 0x400>;
        interrupts = <GIC_SPI <irq> IRQ_TYPE_LEVEL_HIGH>;
        clocks = <&cpg CPG_MOD <clk-id>>;
        resets = <&cpg <reset-id>>;
        power-domains = <&cpg>;
        status = "okay";
    };
};

On the board, after loading:

dmesg | grep mydrv
cat /sys/bus/platform/devices/10049c00.mydrv/reg0

docs.title: Build the module in Yocto
docs.text:
Based on poky's meta-skeleton/recipes-kernel/hello-mod. Layout in my layer:

recipes-kernel/hello-mod/
├── hello-mod_1.0.bb
└── files/
    ├── Makefile
    └── hello.c

The Makefile must use KERNEL_SRC and provide modules_install:

obj-m := hello.o

SRC := $(shell pwd)

all:
	$(MAKE) -C $(KERNEL_SRC) M=$(SRC)

modules_install:
	$(MAKE) -C $(KERNEL_SRC) M=$(SRC) modules_install

clean:
	rm -f *.o *~ core .depend .*.cmd *.ko *.mod.c *.mod
	rm -f Module.markers Module.symvers modules.order
	rm -rf .tmp_versions Modules.symvers

hello-mod_1.0.bb:

DunfellKirkstone and later 
SUMMARY = "Hello world kernel module"
LICENSE = "GPL-2.0"
LIC_FILES_CHKSUM = "file://${COMMON_LICENSE_DIR}/GPL-2.0;md5=801f80980d171dd6425610833a22dbe6"

inherit module

SRC_URI = "file://Makefile file://hello.c"
S = "${WORKDIR}"

RPROVIDES_${PN} += "kernel-module-hello"

SUMMARY = "Hello world kernel module"
LICENSE = "GPL-2.0-only"
LIC_FILES_CHKSUM = "file://${COMMON_LICENSE_DIR}/GPL-2.0-only;md5=801f80980d171dd6425610833a22dbe6"

inherit module

SRC_URI = "file://Makefile file://hello.c"
S = "${WORKDIR}"

RPROVIDES:${PN} += "kernel-module-hello"

Add to the image with IMAGE_INSTALL_append = " hello-mod" (Kirkstone+: IMAGE_INSTALL:append), and autoload it with KERNEL_MODULE_AUTOLOAD += "hello" in the recipe.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause / fix insmod: ERROR: could not insert module: Invalid module format Built against a different kernel. Compare modinfo hello.ko \| grep vermagic with uname -r Unknown symbol in module Missing dependency module or symbol not exported (EXPORT_SYMBOL_GPL). Check dmesg for the symbol name No rule to make target 'modules' / Kernel configuration is invalid KDIR points to an unconfigured or unbuilt tree. Run make defconfig && make modules_prepare in it Driver loads but probe never runs compatible mismatch, or node status not okay. Compare with /proc/device-tree module verification failed: signature and/or required key missing - tainting kernel Warning only, the module still loads

docs.title: Patches
docs.text: Creating, checking and applying patches for the kernel (same commands for U-Boot and TF-A trees).

docs.title: Variables
docs.text:
export KSRC=~/work/rz_linux-cip
export BASE=<base-commit>          # commit my work starts from, e.g. the Yocto SRCREV
export OUT=~/work/patches
export BSP_DIR=~/yocto/rzg2l_vlp_v3.0.x   # only for moving patches into Yocto

docs.title: Commit in kernel style
docs.text:
cd $KSRC
git add -p
git commit -s

Message format:

arm64: dts: renesas: rzg2l-smarc: Enable SPI1

Enable RSPI1 on the PMOD connector and add the pin configuration.

Signed-off-by: Nhat Tran <you@example.com>
  • Subject: subsystem: component: Short description, under ~72 characters. Look at how others did it: git log --oneline -- <file>.
  • -s adds the Signed-off-by line.

Fix the last commit:

git commit --amend

Fix an older commit in the series:

git commit --fixup=<commit>
git rebase -i --autosquash $BASE

docs.title: Create patches
docs.text:
All commits since BASE, one file per commit:

rm -rf $OUT && git format-patch $BASE -o $OUT
ls $OUT

0001-arm64-dts-renesas-rzg2l-smarc-Enable-SPI1.patch
0002-spi-rspi-Fix-xxx.patch

Only the last N commits:

git format-patch -3 -o $OUT

A second version of a series, with a cover letter:

git format-patch -v2 --cover-letter $BASE -o $OUT

docs.title: Check patches
docs.text:
Style check (the kernel's own tool):

./scripts/checkpatch.pl --strict $OUT/*.patch

Check a commit directly, without creating files:

./scripts/checkpatch.pl --strict -g HEAD

Who to send the patch to (upstream submissions):

./scripts/get_maintainer.pl $OUT/0001-*.patch

docs.title: Apply patches
docs.text:
With git (keeps author, message and date):

git am $OUT/*.patch

Test whether patches apply, without changing anything:

git apply --check $OUT/*.patch

Without git, e.g. in an extracted source tarball:

patch -p1 --dry-run < 0001-xxx.patch
patch -p1 < 0001-xxx.patch

docs.title: When git am fails
docs.text:
git am --3way $OUT/*.patch        # retry using the common ancestor; often resolves context drift

If it still stops with a conflict:

git status                        # see conflicting files
# edit and fix conflict markers
git add <fixed files>
git am --continue

Other options:

git am --skip                     # drop the current patch
git am --abort                    # go back to the state before git am

Apply what can be applied and leave .rej files for the rest:

git apply --reject $OUT/0002-*.patch
find . -name "*.rej"

docs.title: Compare two versions of a series
docs.text:
Shows what changed between v1 and v2, commit by commit:

git range-diff $BASE..work-v1 $BASE..work-v2

docs.title: Move patches into Yocto
docs.text:
Copy them into my layer and list them in the .bbappend (see Custom layer & bbappend):

cp $OUT/*.patch $BSP_DIR/meta-mylayer/recipes-kernel/linux/files/

Generate the SRC_URI lines:

for p in $OUT/*.patch; do echo "    file://$(basename $p) \\"; done

Tip

Patches must apply on the exact source the recipe uses (SRCREV plus the BSP's own patches). Making them with devtool guarantees that.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause / fix patch does not apply Base differs. Use git am --3way, or rebase my commits onto the target base and regenerate Patch is empty Commit already exists in the tree. git am --skip git am reports previous rebase directory .git/rebase-apply still exists A previous git am was not finished. git am --abort Yocto do_patch fails after BSP upgrade Kernel moved on. devtool modify, re-apply with git am --3way, then devtool finish

docs.title: U-Boot
docs.text:
U-Boot notes for RZ boards. How to write U-Boot itself to QSPI is in Flashing the bootloader.

Article When to use it Environment presets Switching between NFS, SD card and eMMC boot with one command U-Boot commands Environment, network, MMC, memory, fdt commands

docs.title: U-Boot commands
docs.text:
Commands I use at the U-Boot prompt (=>). Stop autoboot by pressing any key during Hit any key to stop autoboot.

Load addresses below are the ones used on RZ/G2L (DDR starts at 0x40000000): kernel 0x48080000, dtb 0x48000000.

docs.title: Help and info
docs.text:
help
help mmc
version
bdinfo

docs.title: Environment
docs.text:
printenv
printenv bootcmd bootargs
setenv myvar 'value with spaces'
setenv myvar                         # delete a variable
editenv bootargs                     # edit in place (no retyping)
saveenv
env default -a                       # reset everything to defaults (then saveenv)

Run a script stored in a variable:

run nfsboot

Set bootdelay (seconds before autoboot; -1 = never autoboot, 0 = no delay but still interruptible by keypress if enabled):

setenv bootdelay 3
saveenv

docs.title: Network
docs.text:
setenv ipaddr 192.168.1.5
setenv serverip 192.168.1.3
ping ${serverip}
tftp 0x48080000 Image
dhcp                                  # get IP from a DHCP server instead

After tftp, ${filesize} holds the number of bytes loaded (hex). Useful for writing the file somewhere else.

docs.title: MMC (SD card / eMMC)
docs.text:
On RZ/G2L SMARC: mmc 0 = eMMC, mmc 1 = micro SD.

mmc list
mmc dev 1
mmc info
mmc part
mmc rescan                            # after inserting a card

docs.title: Filesystems
docs.text:
ext4:

ext4ls mmc 1:1
ext4ls mmc 1:2 /boot
ext4load mmc 1:1 0x48080000 Image

FAT:

fatls mmc 1:1
fatload mmc 1:1 0x48080000 Image

Generic (filesystem type detected automatically):

ls mmc 1:1
load mmc 1:1 0x48080000 Image

docs.title: USB storage
docs.text:
usb start
usb storage
ls usb 0:1
load usb 0:1 0x48080000 Image

docs.title: Memory
docs.text:
Display (md), write (mw), copy (cp), compare (cmp):

md.l 0x48000000 0x20                  # 0x20 words of 32 bit
mw.l 0x48000000 0xdeadbeef 1
cp.b 0x48080000 0x50000000 ${filesize}
cmp.b 0x48080000 0x50000000 ${filesize}

Peek a peripheral register (read-only check, e.g. a pin function register):

md.l <register-address> 1

Warning

Writing peripheral registers with mw can hang the board. Prefer md for checks.

docs.title: Device tree in RAM
docs.text:
After loading the dtb, inspect or modify it before booting:

fdt addr 0x48000000
fdt print /chosen
fdt print /soc/serial@1004b800
fdt list /
fdt set /soc/spi@1004b000 status "okay"
fdt resize 8192                       # make room before adding nodes or applying overlays

docs.title: Boot
docs.text:
booti 0x48080000 - 0x48000000         # arm64 Image, no initramfs, dtb
booti 0x48080000 0x49000000:${filesize} 0x48000000   # with initramfs
boot                                  # run bootcmd
reset

docs.title: Scripting
docs.text:
Conditionals, useful inside stored scripts:

if ping ${serverip}; then run nfsboot; else run sdboot; fi

if test -e mmc 1:1 Image; then echo "Image found on SD"; fi

docs.title: QSPI flash
docs.text:
The bootloaders are in QSPI. Read only; writing is done with Flash Writer (Flashing the bootloader):

sf probe
sf read 0x48000000 0x0 0x1000
md.b 0x48000000 0x40

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause / fix Unknown command 'ext4load' Command not built into this U-Boot. Try the generic load ** Bad device specification mmc 1 ** No card, or wrong device number. mmc list, mmc rescan TFTP error: trying to overwrite reserved memory Load address overlaps U-Boot itself. Use the standard addresses above Bad Linux ARM64 Image magic! File loaded is not an arm64 Image (wrong file, or a compressed Image.gz), or loaded to a different address than booti uses ERROR: Did not find a cmdline Flattened Device Tree dtb not loaded, or loaded to another address than given to booti

docs.title: Environment presets
docs.text:
Instead of retyping bootcmd and bootargs every time I switch boot method, I store each method as a named script in the U-Boot environment. Switching is then one run command.

The individual boot methods are explained in Booting with TFTP and NFS and Booting from SD Card and eMMC. This page only combines them.

docs.title: 1. Common settings
docs.text:
Board-specific values, set once. Values below are for RZ/G2L SMARC; change fdtfile for other boards.

setenv ipaddr 192.168.1.5
setenv serverip 192.168.1.3
setenv netmask 255.255.255.0
setenv nfsdir /nfs/rzg2l
setenv kernel Image
setenv fdtfile r9a07g044l2-smarc.dtb
setenv k_addr 0x48080000
setenv fdt_addr 0x48000000
setenv args_common 'console=ttySC0,115200n8 rootwait rw noinitrd nohlt panic=1 earlyprintk=ttySC0,115200n8'

Note

ethaddr (MAC address) is usually already set from the board. If printenv ethaddr shows nothing, set it once with setenv ethaddr xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx. U-Boot allows setting it only once; changing it later needs env default -a.

docs.title: 2. Boot scripts
docs.text:
Copy these three lines as they are. The single quotes keep ${...} unexpanded until the script runs, so later changes to the common settings take effect.

TFTP kernel + NFS rootfs:

setenv nfsboot 'setenv bootargs ${args_common} ip=${ipaddr}:${serverip}::${netmask}::eth0 root=/dev/nfs nfsroot=${serverip}:${nfsdir},nfsvers=3,tcp; tftp ${k_addr} ${kernel}; tftp ${fdt_addr} ${fdtfile}; booti ${k_addr} - ${fdt_addr}'

SD card (partition 1: kernel + dtb, partition 2: rootfs):

setenv sdboot 'setenv bootargs ${args_common} root=/dev/mmcblk1p2; mmc dev 1; ext4load mmc 1:1 ${k_addr} ${kernel}; ext4load mmc 1:1 ${fdt_addr} ${fdtfile}; booti ${k_addr} - ${fdt_addr}'

eMMC (same layout):

setenv emmcboot 'setenv bootargs ${args_common} root=/dev/mmcblk0p2; mmc dev 0; ext4load mmc 0:1 ${k_addr} ${kernel}; ext4load mmc 0:1 ${fdt_addr} ${fdtfile}; booti ${k_addr} - ${fdt_addr}'

Optional: TFTP kernel + rootfs on the SD card. Useful when only the kernel changes and the SD rootfs is fine:

setenv tftpsd 'setenv bootargs ${args_common} root=/dev/mmcblk1p2; tftp ${k_addr} ${kernel}; tftp ${fdt_addr} ${fdtfile}; booti ${k_addr} - ${fdt_addr}'

docs.title: 3. Choose the default and save
docs.text:
setenv bootcmd 'run nfsboot'
saveenv

docs.title: Switching
docs.text:
Permanently switch the default boot method:

setenv bootcmd 'run sdboot'
saveenv

Boot another method once, without changing the default (stop autoboot first):

run emmcboot

Check what is stored:

printenv bootcmd nfsboot sdboot emmcboot

docs.title: Reset to factory environment
docs.text:
env default -a
saveenv

This removes all presets above, and ethaddr if it is not stored elsewhere.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause / fix Characters missing after pasting a long setenv line The serial console drops characters on fast paste. In Tera Term set Setup → Serial port → Transmit delay to 1–5 ms/char, or paste line by line ## Error: "nfsboot" not defined The script was not saved, or env default -a was run. Set it again and saveenv Variables expanded too early (fixed IPs inside the script) Script was set with double quotes. Use single quotes Can't overwrite "ethaddr" MAC can be set only once. env default -a, then set it again Kernel panics VFS: Unable to mount root fs Wrong root= for the chosen medium. Compare printenv bootargs after run with the partition layout
