docs.text:
Bring-up and development notes for the Renesas RZ/V2N Evaluation Board Kit.

Device tree: r9a09g056n48-rzv2n-evk.dtb

docs.title: Yocto
docs.text:
Notes on building the Renesas RZ BSP with Yocto: preparing the host, building images, customizing with my own layer, and producing an SDK.

Article When to use it Host setup Once per build machine Build the BSP Fresh build of a BSP release Build output Finding Image, dtb, rootfs, bootloaders after a build BitBake commands Daily rebuild / inspect commands Custom layer & bbappend Adding my own recipes, patches, kernel config devtool Editing a recipe's source (kernel, U-Boot) and turning it into patches SDK Cross-compiling outside Yocto

docs.title: BitBake commands
docs.text: Commands I use daily inside the build environment (source poky/oe-init-build-env build).

docs.title: Variables
docs.text:
export RECIPE=linux-renesas     # recipe to work on
export IMAGE=core-image-minimal

Recipe names in the Renesas BSP:

Component Recipe Kernel linux-renesas (also reachable as virtual/kernel) U-Boot u-boot TF-A (BL2, BL31, FIP) trusted-firmware-a Flash Writer flash-writer

Override syntax: Dunfell vs. Kirkstone and later

Dunfell (Yocto 3.1, used by RZ/G2L VLP 3.0.x) uses an underscore: IMAGE_INSTALL_append, SRC_URI_append, FILESEXTRAPATHS_prepend. Kirkstone (4.0) and later use a colon: IMAGE_INSTALL:append, SRC_URI:append, FILESEXTRAPATHS:prepend. Using the wrong one is silently ignored or raises a parse error, so match the BSP's Yocto version.

docs.title: Build and rebuild
docs.text:
Build one recipe (and its dependencies):

bitbake $RECIPE

Force a task to run again even if BitBake thinks it is up to date:

bitbake $RECIPE -c compile -f
bitbake $RECIPE

Re-run from a task onward (capital -C invalidates the task and everything after it):

bitbake $RECIPE -C compile

Clean levels, from light to heavy:

bitbake $RECIPE -c clean          # remove work dir; sstate still used
bitbake $RECIPE -c cleansstate    # also remove sstate -> real rebuild from source
bitbake $RECIPE -c cleanall       # also remove downloaded source -> refetch

Keep going after an error, to see all failing recipes at once:

bitbake -k $IMAGE

List the tasks of a recipe:

bitbake $RECIPE -c listtasks

docs.title: Inspect variables
docs.text:
Print the final value of a variable after all .bbappend and overrides:

bitbake -e $RECIPE | grep ^SRC_URI=
bitbake -e $RECIPE | grep ^WORKDIR=
bitbake -e $IMAGE  | grep ^IMAGE_INSTALL=

Show where a variable was set or changed (history):

bitbake -e $RECIPE | less     # search for "# $SRC_URI" to see every assignment

docs.title: Find things
docs.text:
Which layer provides a recipe, and which version:

bitbake-layers show-recipes "$RECIPE"
bitbake-layers show-recipes "*u-boot*"

All .bbappend files applied to recipes:

bitbake-layers show-appends | grep -A5 $RECIPE

Layers and their priorities:

bitbake-layers show-layers

Find the recipe file on disk:

find .. -name "${RECIPE}*.bb" -not -path "*/tmp/*"

docs.title: Packages and files
docs.text:
Which package installs a file (needs a finished build):

oe-pkgdata-util find-path /usr/sbin/i2cdetect

Which recipe produces a package, and what files a package contains:

oe-pkgdata-util lookup-recipe i2c-tools
oe-pkgdata-util list-pkg-files i2c-tools

Add packages to the image, in conf/local.conf:

DunfellKirkstone and later 
IMAGE_INSTALL_append = " i2c-tools can-utils devmem2 ethtool"

IMAGE_INSTALL:append = " i2c-tools can-utils devmem2 ethtool"

Warning

Keep the leading space inside the quotes. _append / :append does not add a separator.

docs.title: Logs and work directory
docs.text:
Each recipe builds in its own WORKDIR:

WORKDIR=$(bitbake -e $RECIPE | sed -n 's/^WORKDIR="\(.*\)"/\1/p'); echo $WORKDIR

Task logs and the exact scripts that ran:

ls $WORKDIR/temp/
less $WORKDIR/temp/log.do_compile
less $WORKDIR/temp/run.do_compile

When a task fails, BitBake prints the log path at the end of the error. That log is the first thing to read.

docs.title: Interactive shell
docs.text:
Open a shell with the recipe's cross-compile environment, in the source directory:

bitbake $RECIPE -c devshell

Useful for trying a make command manually. Changes made here are lost on the next clean, so use devtool for real changes.

docs.title: Kernel-specific tasks
docs.text:
bitbake virtual/kernel -c menuconfig      # interactive config
bitbake virtual/kernel -c diffconfig      # write changes as a config fragment
bitbake virtual/kernel -c savedefconfig   # write a minimal defconfig
bitbake virtual/kernel -c kernel_configcheck -f

diffconfig and savedefconfig print the output path. Use the fragment in a .bbappend to keep the change.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
Why is a package in my image? Generate dependency files and search them:

bitbake -g $IMAGE
grep '"i2c-tools"' task-depends.dot | head

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause / fix Change in a .bbappend has no effect Wrong override syntax for the Yocto version, or layer not in bblayers.conf. Verify with bitbake -e Taskhash mismatch / basehash errors Corrupt sstate or a non-deterministic recipe. bitbake $RECIPE -c cleansstate and rebuild ERROR: Unable to start bitbake server A previous BitBake is still running or crashed. Wait, or remove bitbake.lock in the build dir Rebuilt the kernel but the image has the old one Rebuild the image too: bitbake $IMAGE

docs.title: Build the BSP
docs.text: Building a Renesas RZ BSP release from scratch, from the release packages to a bootable image.

docs.title: Variables
docs.text:
Set these first. Every command below uses them.

export BSP_DIR=~/yocto/rzg2l_vlp_v3.0.x      # where the BSP is extracted
export MACHINE=smarc-rzg2l                   # see the machine table below
export IMAGE=core-image-minimal              # or core-image-weston
Board MACHINE RZ/G2L SMARC EVK smarc-rzg2l RZ/G2LC SMARC EVK smarc-rzg2lc RZ/G2UL SMARC EVK smarc-rzg2ul RZ/V2L SMARC EVK smarc-rzv2l RZ/G3S SMARC EVK smarc-rzg3s RZ/G3E SMARC EVK smarc-rzg3e RZ/V2N EVK rzv2n-evk

docs.title: Release packages
docs.text:
A BSP release from renesas.com is a set of zip files:

Package Content BSP (VLP) poky, meta-openembedded, meta-renesas, other base layers, and an offline oss_pkg download archive Graphics library meta-rz-graphics (GPU driver, needed for core-image-weston) Video codec library meta-rz-codecs (hardware video encode/decode)

Graphics and codec packages are optional for core-image-minimal, and required for core-image-weston with GPU acceleration.

docs.title: Extract
docs.text:
mkdir -p $BSP_DIR && cd $BSP_DIR
unzip <path>/RTK0EF0045Z0021AZJ-v3.0.x.zip
tar -xf rzg_vlp_v3.0.x.tar.gz

Optional graphics and codec layers (they extract into meta-rz-features/):

cd $BSP_DIR
unzip <path>/<graphics-package>.zip
tar -xf meta-rz-features_graphics_v*.tar.gz
unzip <path>/<codec-package>.zip
tar -xf meta-rz-features_codec_v*.tar.gz

Note

The exact archive names change between releases. Check ls after each unzip and follow the release note's file list.

Check the layers:

ls $BSP_DIR

meta-gplv2  meta-openembedded  meta-qt5  meta-renesas  meta-rz-features  meta-virtualization  poky

docs.title: Create the build directory
docs.text:
TEMPLATECONF points to the Renesas template for local.conf and bblayers.conf:

RZ/G2L family (VLP 3.0.x, Dunfell)Older VLP (1.x) 
cd $BSP_DIR
TEMPLATECONF=$PWD/meta-renesas/meta-rz-common/docs/template/conf/ \
    source poky/oe-init-build-env build

cd $BSP_DIR
TEMPLATECONF=$PWD/meta-renesas/meta-rzg2l/docs/template/conf/ \
    source poky/oe-init-build-env build

The shell is now in $BSP_DIR/build. In every new terminal, re-enter the build environment with (no TEMPLATECONF needed any more):

cd $BSP_DIR && source poky/oe-init-build-env build

TODO

Newer BSPs for RZ/G3E and RZ/V2N use a different TEMPLATECONF path. Copy the exact line from that BSP's release note into a new tab here.

docs.title: Add optional layers
docs.text:
bitbake-layers add-layer ../meta-rz-features/meta-rz-graphics
bitbake-layers add-layer ../meta-rz-features/meta-rz-codecs
bitbake-layers show-layers

docs.title: Edit local.conf
docs.text:
Append to conf/local.conf:

cat >> conf/local.conf << EOF

# --- my settings ---
MACHINE = "${MACHINE}"
DL_DIR = "\${HOME}/yocto/downloads"
SSTATE_DIR = "\${HOME}/yocto/sstate-cache"
BB_NUMBER_THREADS = "8"
PARALLEL_MAKE = "-j 8"
# remove work files after each recipe is built (saves a lot of disk)
INHERIT += "rm_work"
RM_WORK_EXCLUDE += "linux-renesas u-boot"
EOF

Tip

RM_WORK_EXCLUDE keeps the kernel and U-Boot work directories, so their source and build tree stay available for inspection and devshell.

docs.title: Offline build
docs.text:
The BSP ships the source tarballs of all packages (oss_pkg, a .7z archive). To build without network access, extract it and copy its content into DL_DIR, then disable fetching:

mkdir -p /tmp/oss_pkg
7z x $BSP_DIR/oss_pkg_rzg_v3.0.x.7z -o/tmp/oss_pkg
ls /tmp/oss_pkg                                   # find the directory holding the tarballs
cp -r /tmp/oss_pkg/<dir>/* ~/yocto/downloads/
echo 'BB_NO_NETWORK = "1"' >> conf/local.conf

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
bitbake $IMAGE

A first build takes 1–4 hours depending on the machine. Later builds reuse the sstate cache and take minutes.

Output files are in tmp/deploy/images/$MACHINE/.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause / fix Nothing PROVIDES 'xxx' A layer is missing. Check bitbake-layers show-layers, add the layer providing the recipe Fetcher failure / Unable to fetch URL No network or server down. Use the offline build archive ERROR: Layer xxx is not compatible with the core layer Layer from a different Yocto release. Use layers from the same BSP release core-image-weston builds but Weston fails to start (no GPU) Graphics layer not added. Add meta-rz-graphics and rebuild Build directory got messed up after changing many settings Delete tmp/ (not sstate-cache) and rebuild; sstate makes it fast

docs.title: Custom layer & bbappend
docs.text: All my changes (kernel patches, config, device tree, my own apps) go into my own layer instead of editing meta-renesas. The BSP layers stay untouched and can be upgraded, and my changes are kept in one place under version control.

docs.title: Variables
docs.text:
export BSP_DIR=~/yocto/rzg2l_vlp_v3.0.x
export LAYER=meta-mylayer

Run everything from the build directory:

cd $BSP_DIR && source poky/oe-init-build-env build

docs.title: Create and add the layer
docs.text:
bitbake-layers create-layer ../$LAYER
bitbake-layers add-layer ../$LAYER
bitbake-layers show-layers | grep mylayer

Generated structure:

meta-mylayer/
├── conf/layer.conf
├── COPYING.MIT
├── README
└── recipes-example/example/example_0.1.bb

Remove the example recipe:

rm -rf ../$LAYER/recipes-example

Check LAYERSERIES_COMPAT in conf/layer.conf matches the BSP's Yocto release:

DunfellKirkstoneScarthgap 
LAYERSERIES_COMPAT_meta-mylayer = "dunfell"

LAYERSERIES_COMPAT_meta-mylayer = "kirkstone"

LAYERSERIES_COMPAT_meta-mylayer = "scarthgap"

docs.title: Kernel: patches and config fragments
docs.text:
Layout:

meta-mylayer/recipes-kernel/linux/
├── linux-renesas_%.bbappend
└── files/
    ├── 0001-arm64-dts-renesas-enable-sci1.patch
    └── my-config.cfg

mkdir -p ../$LAYER/recipes-kernel/linux/files

linux-renesas_%.bbappend (the % matches any recipe version):

DunfellKirkstone and later 
FILESEXTRAPATHS_prepend := "${THISDIR}/files:"

SRC_URI_append = " \
    file://0001-arm64-dts-renesas-enable-sci1.patch \
    file://my-config.cfg \
"

FILESEXTRAPATHS:prepend := "${THISDIR}/files:"

SRC_URI:append = " \
    file://0001-arm64-dts-renesas-enable-sci1.patch \
    file://my-config.cfg \
"

my-config.cfg holds only the options to change, in .config syntax:

CONFIG_SPI_SPIDEV=y
CONFIG_CAN_RCAR_CANFD=y
# CONFIG_DEBUG_INFO is not set

Rebuild and verify:

bitbake linux-renesas -c cleansstate && bitbake linux-renesas
grep -E "SPIDEV|CANFD" tmp/work/*/linux-renesas/*/build/.config

Tip

Patches are applied with git am/patch in the order they appear in SRC_URI. Generate them with git format-patch from a kernel tree, or let devtool finish write them for you.

Warning

If an option in a .cfg does not appear in the final .config, its dependencies are not met. BitBake prints a warning during do_kernel_configcheck. Find the missing dependency with menuconfig (search with /).

docs.title: U-Boot: patches
docs.text:
Same pattern, recipe name u-boot:

mkdir -p ../$LAYER/recipes-bsp/u-boot/files

recipes-bsp/u-boot/u-boot_%.bbappend:

DunfellKirkstone and later 
FILESEXTRAPATHS_prepend := "${THISDIR}/files:"
SRC_URI_append = " file://0001-change-default-bootcmd.patch"

FILESEXTRAPATHS:prepend := "${THISDIR}/files:"
SRC_URI:append = " file://0001-change-default-bootcmd.patch"

docs.title: My own application recipe
docs.text:
Layout:

meta-mylayer/recipes-apps/hello/
├── hello_1.0.bb
└── files/hello.c

mkdir -p ../$LAYER/recipes-apps/hello/files

files/hello.c:

#include <stdio.h>

int main(void)
{
    printf("Hello from RZ\n");
    return 0;
}

hello_1.0.bb:

SUMMARY = "Hello world test application"
LICENSE = "MIT"
LIC_FILES_CHKSUM = "file://${COMMON_LICENSE_DIR}/MIT;md5=0835ade698e0bcf8506ecda2f7b4f302"

SRC_URI = "file://hello.c"
S = "${WORKDIR}"

do_compile() {
    ${CC} ${CFLAGS} ${LDFLAGS} hello.c -o hello
}

do_install() {
    install -d ${D}${bindir}
    install -m 0755 hello ${D}${bindir}/
}

Note

Always use ${CC} ${CFLAGS} ${LDFLAGS}. Calling gcc directly builds for the host, and leaving out ${LDFLAGS} causes a QA Issue: No GNU_HASH in the ELF binary error.

Build it, then add it to the image:

bitbake hello
DunfellKirkstone and later 
IMAGE_INSTALL_append = " hello"

IMAGE_INSTALL:append = " hello"

docs.title: Install a file into the rootfs
docs.text:
For config files or scripts that are not built, e.g. /etc/profile.d/myenv.sh:

recipes-core/myfiles/myfiles_1.0.bb:

SUMMARY = "My rootfs files"
LICENSE = "MIT"
LIC_FILES_CHKSUM = "file://${COMMON_LICENSE_DIR}/MIT;md5=0835ade698e0bcf8506ecda2f7b4f302"

SRC_URI = "file://myenv.sh"
S = "${WORKDIR}"

do_install() {
    install -d ${D}${sysconfdir}/profile.d
    install -m 0644 myenv.sh ${D}${sysconfdir}/profile.d/
}

docs.title: My own image recipe
docs.text:
Instead of growing local.conf, define an image in the layer.

recipes-core/images/my-image.bb:

require recipes-core/images/core-image-minimal.bb

SUMMARY = "Development image for RZ boards"

IMAGE_INSTALL_append = " \
    hello \
    i2c-tools \
    can-utils \
    ethtool \
    openssh \
"

IMAGE_FEATURES += "ssh-server-openssh debug-tweaks tools-debug"

(For Kirkstone and later, replace IMAGE_INSTALL_append with IMAGE_INSTALL:append.)

bitbake my-image

Warning

debug-tweaks allows root login without a password. Use it only for development images.

docs.title: Keep the layer in git
docs.text:
cd ../$LAYER
git init
git add .
git commit -m "Initial layer"

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause / fix No recipes available for: .../linux-renesas_%.bbappend File name does not match the recipe name. Check with bitbake-layers show-recipes linux-renesas Unable to get checksum for ... file://xxx File not found. Check FILESEXTRAPATHS and that the file is in files/ Patch fails: Hunk #1 FAILED Patch made against a different kernel version. Regenerate it from the recipe's source (devtool modify) Layer ... is not compatible with the core layer Fix LAYERSERIES_COMPAT in layer.conf QA Issue: ... already-stripped Recipe strips the binary itself. Remove -s from the build or add INSANE_SKIP_${PN} = "already-stripped" (Kirkstone and later: INSANE_SKIP:${PN})

docs.title: Build output
docs.text: Where the build results are, which file is used for what, and how to copy them to the TFTP/NFS server or an SD card.

docs.title: Variables
docs.text:
export BSP_DIR=~/yocto/rzg2l_vlp_v3.0.x
export MACHINE=smarc-rzg2l
export IMAGE=core-image-minimal
export DEPLOY=$BSP_DIR/build/tmp/deploy/images/$MACHINE

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
ls -l $DEPLOY

Files for RZ/G2L SMARC (other boards follow the same pattern with their own names):

File Used for Image Kernel. Loaded by U-Boot (TFTP, SD, eMMC) r9a07g044l2-smarc.dtb Device tree for the board modules-$MACHINE.tgz Kernel modules (/lib/modules/...), already included in the rootfs $IMAGE-$MACHINE.tar.bz2 Root filesystem as a tarball. Extract to NFS export or an SD/eMMC partition $IMAGE-$MACHINE.ext4 Root filesystem as an ext4 image $IMAGE-$MACHINE.wic.* Full disk image (partitions + kernel + rootfs). Write directly to an SD card $IMAGE-$MACHINE.wic.bmap Block map for fast writing with bmaptool Flash_Writer_SCIF_*.mot Flash Writer, sent over SCIF in SCIF download mode bl2_bp-*.srec, fip-*.srec Bootloaders (TF-A BL2, FIP = BL31 + U-Boot) for writing to QSPI bl2_bp-*.bin, fip-*.bin Same bootloaders in binary form (eMMC boot partitions)

Which bootloader files to use is described in Flashing the bootloader.

Note

The compressed format of .wic (.wic.gz, .wic.xz, .wic.bz2) depends on IMAGE_FSTYPES in the BSP. Check with:

bitbake -e $IMAGE | grep ^IMAGE_FSTYPES=

docs.title: Symlinks vs. timestamped files
docs.text:
Each build creates timestamped files (for example core-image-minimal-smarc-rzg2l-20261017081530.rootfs.tar.bz2) plus a stable symlink pointing to the latest one. Always use the symlink names, and copy with -L so the real file is copied, not the link:

cp -L $DEPLOY/Image /some/where/

Old timestamped files pile up over many builds. Remove ones older than 7 days:

find $DEPLOY -maxdepth 1 -type f -name "*-20[0-9]*" -mtime +7 -delete

docs.title: Copy to TFTP / NFS server
docs.text:
Matches the setup in Booting with TFTP and NFS:

sudo cp -L $DEPLOY/Image $DEPLOY/r9a07g044l2-smarc.dtb /srv/tftp/

Replace the NFS rootfs with the new one:

sudo rm -rf /nfs/rzg2l/*
sudo tar -xf $DEPLOY/$IMAGE-$MACHINE.tar.bz2 -C /nfs/rzg2l

Warning

Double-check the path in rm -rf. An empty or wrong variable here can delete the host's files.

docs.title: Copy to an SD card on the host
docs.text:
Write the full .wic image (all partitions at once):

lsblk                                   # find the SD card, e.g. /dev/sdb
export SDCARD=/dev/sdX
sudo umount ${SDCARD}* 2>/dev/null
sudo bmaptool copy $DEPLOY/$IMAGE-$MACHINE.wic.gz $SDCARD

Without bmaptool, decompress and use dd (slower, writes empty blocks too):

gunzip -c $DEPLOY/$IMAGE-$MACHINE.wic.gz | sudo dd of=$SDCARD bs=4M conv=fsync status=progress

To build my own partition layout instead, see Booting from SD Card and eMMC.

docs.title: SDK output
docs.text:
bitbake $IMAGE -c populate_sdk writes the SDK installer to a different directory:

ls $BSP_DIR/build/tmp/deploy/sdk/

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause / fix Copied Image is only a few bytes A symlink was copied. Use cp -L Board still runs the old kernel Copied to the wrong TFTP directory, or U-Boot loads from SD/eMMC. Check printenv bootcmd No .wic file wic is not in IMAGE_FSTYPES. Add IMAGE_FSTYPES:append = " wic.gz wic.bmap" (Dunfell syntax: IMAGE_FSTYPES_append)

docs.title: devtool
docs.text: devtool checks out a recipe's source into a git workspace, builds the recipe from there, and at the end turns my commits into patches inside my layer. This is how I modify the kernel or U-Boot within Yocto.

docs.title: Variables
docs.text:
export BSP_DIR=~/yocto/rzg2l_vlp_v3.0.x
export RECIPE=linux-renesas          # or u-boot, trusted-firmware-a
export LAYER=../meta-mylayer         # destination layer, relative to build/
export MACHINE=smarc-rzg2l
export BOARD_IP=192.168.1.5

cd $BSP_DIR && source poky/oe-init-build-env build

docs.title: Workflow overview
docs.text:
devtool modify  ->  edit + git commit  ->  bitbake / devtool build  ->  test on board
       ^                                                                     |
       +----------------------------- repeat --------------------------------+
                                       |
                                devtool finish  ->  patches + .bbappend in my layer

docs.title: 1. Check out the source
docs.text:
devtool modify $RECIPE

The source (with all BSP patches already applied) is now a git repository at:

cd $BSP_DIR/build/workspace/sources/$RECIPE
git log --oneline -5
git branch        # work happens on branch "devtool"

From now on BitBake builds this recipe from the workspace, not from the original source.

docs.title: 2. Edit and commit
docs.text:
Edit files normally, then commit. Each commit becomes one patch:

cd $BSP_DIR/build/workspace/sources/$RECIPE
git add -A
git commit -s -m "arm64: dts: renesas: rzg2l-smarc: enable SCI1"

Tip

Use kernel-style commit subjects (subsystem: component: what). They become the patch file names, e.g. 0001-arm64-dts-renesas-rzg2l-smarc-enable-SCI1.patch.

docs.title: 3. Build
docs.text:
cd $BSP_DIR/build
bitbake $RECIPE

For the kernel, this also runs do_deploy, so the new Image and dtb land in tmp/deploy/images/$MACHINE/. Copy them to TFTP for a quick test:

sudo cp -L tmp/deploy/images/$MACHINE/Image tmp/deploy/images/$MACHINE/*.dtb /srv/tftp/

Note

devtool build $RECIPE also works, but stops before do_deploy. For the kernel, bitbake $RECIPE is more convenient because the output ends up in the deploy directory.

docs.title: Kernel config through devtool
docs.text:
devtool menuconfig linux-renesas

The changes are saved as oe-local-files/devtool-fragment.cfg in the workspace and included by devtool finish.

docs.title: Applications: deploy directly to the board
docs.text:
For user-space recipes, install the build result on a running board over SSH:

devtool build hello
devtool deploy-target hello root@$BOARD_IP
# remove it again
devtool undeploy-target hello root@$BOARD_IP

docs.title: 4. Finish: write patches into my layer
docs.text:
devtool finish $RECIPE $LAYER

This:

  • writes each commit as a patch to $LAYER/recipes-.../<recipe>/files/ (or a version-named directory),
  • creates or updates the .bbappend with SRC_URI entries for the patches,
  • removes the recipe from the workspace, so BitBake builds from the original source + patches again.

Check what was written:

cd $LAYER && git status && git diff

Warning

devtool finish fails if the workspace has uncommitted changes. Commit or git stash first.

docs.title: Other useful commands
docs.text:
devtool status                         # recipes currently in the workspace
devtool update-recipe -a $LAYER $RECIPE   # write patches but keep working in the workspace
devtool reset $RECIPE                  # drop the workspace, discard changes (source dir is kept)
devtool add hello https://github.com/<user>/hello.git    # new recipe from a git repo
devtool upgrade $RECIPE -V <version>   # move a recipe to a newer upstream version

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause / fix ERROR: recipe xxx is already in your workspace A previous devtool modify was never finished. devtool reset $RECIPE, or keep working in the existing workspace Source tree path ... already exists and is not empty after reset devtool reset keeps the source. Delete workspace/sources/$RECIPE or use devtool modify $RECIPE <other-dir> Changes not in the build Not committed? BitBake builds the working tree, but finish only exports commits. Also check devtool status Patches written to the wrong layer Pass the layer path explicitly to devtool finish, and check the layer is in bblayers.conf

docs.title: Host setup
docs.text: Preparing an Ubuntu machine (native or VM) to build the RZ BSP.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Item Recommended OS Ubuntu 20.04 for Dunfell-based BSPs (RZ/G2L VLP 3.0.x), Ubuntu 22.04 for Kirkstone/Scarthgap-based BSPs Disk 150 GB free or more (a core-image-weston build with SDK uses ~100 GB) RAM 16 GB or more, plus swap CPU As many cores as possible; build time scales almost linearly

Tip

The supported host distro is listed in the release note of each BSP. When the host is newer than supported, BitBake prints a warning (Host distribution "ubuntu-24.04" has not been validated). It usually still works, but use the supported version, or a container (see below), when you hit strange host-tool errors.

docs.title: Install packages
docs.text:
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y gawk wget git diffstat unzip texinfo gcc build-essential \
    chrpath socat cpio python3 python3-pip python3-pexpect xz-utils debianutils \
    iputils-ping python3-git python3-jinja2 python3-subunit zstd liblz4-tool file \
    locales libacl1 libsdl1.2-dev xterm p7zip-full libyaml-dev libssl-dev bmap-tools

Note

On Ubuntu 20.04, liblz4-tool provides lz4c; on 22.04 and later the package is lz4. Install whichever exists.

docs.title: Locale
docs.text:
BitBake requires a UTF-8 locale:

sudo locale-gen en_US.UTF-8
sudo update-locale LANG=en_US.UTF-8

docs.title: Git identity
docs.text:
Some recipes apply patches with git am, which fails without an identity:

git config --global user.name "Your Name"
git config --global user.email "you@example.com"

docs.title: Increase inotify limits
docs.text:
Avoids No space left on device errors from file watchers (the disk is not actually full) during large builds:

echo "fs.inotify.max_user_watches=524288" | sudo tee /etc/sysctl.d/99-yocto.conf
sudo sysctl --system

docs.title: Shared download and sstate directories
docs.text:
Keep downloads and the shared state cache outside any single build tree, so several BSP builds can reuse them:

mkdir -p ~/yocto/downloads ~/yocto/sstate-cache

These directories are referenced from local.conf when building the BSP.

docs.title: Optional: build inside a container
docs.text:
When the host Ubuntu version differs from what the BSP supports, build in a container of the supported version:

docker run --rm -it \
    -v ~/yocto:/home/build/yocto \
    -w /home/build/yocto \
    crops/poky:ubuntu-20.04

crops/poky images already contain all required packages and run as a non-root user matching the mounted directory owner.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause / fix Please use a locale setting which supports UTF-8 Run the Locale step and open a new shell Do not use Bitbake as root Build as a normal user, never with sudo Host distribution ... has not been validated Warning only; use a container if the build fails in host tools Build killed randomly / c++: fatal error: Killed signal Out of memory. Lower BB_NUMBER_THREADS / PARALLEL_MAKE or add swap No space left on device with free disk Raise inotify limits, or check df -i for exhausted inodes

docs.title: SDK
docs.text: The SDK is a self-contained cross toolchain plus a sysroot matching the image. With it I can build applications, kernel modules and even the kernel without running BitBake.

docs.title: Variables
docs.text:
export BSP_DIR=~/yocto/rzg2l_vlp_v3.0.x
export IMAGE=core-image-minimal
export SDK_DIR=/opt/poky/3.1.x           # install location; one directory per SDK
export BOARD_IP=192.168.1.5

docs.title: Build the SDK installer
docs.text:
Build the SDK from the same image that runs on the board, so the libraries match:

cd $BSP_DIR && source poky/oe-init-build-env build
bitbake $IMAGE -c populate_sdk
ls tmp/deploy/sdk/

poky-glibc-x86_64-core-image-minimal-aarch64-smarc-rzg2l-toolchain-3.1.x.sh

docs.title: Extra content in the SDK
docs.text:
Add to conf/local.conf before building the SDK, if needed:

DunfellKirkstone and later 
# kernel source for building out-of-tree modules
TOOLCHAIN_TARGET_TASK_append = " kernel-devsrc"
# cmake on the host side
TOOLCHAIN_HOST_TASK_append = " nativesdk-cmake"

TOOLCHAIN_TARGET_TASK:append = " kernel-devsrc"
TOOLCHAIN_HOST_TASK:append = " nativesdk-cmake"

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
sudo sh tmp/deploy/sdk/poky-glibc-x86_64-$IMAGE-*-toolchain-*.sh -d $SDK_DIR -y

Tip

Install SDKs for different BSPs or boards into different directories (/opt/poky/rzg2l-3.1.x, /opt/poky/rzv2n-5.0, ...). Sourcing two environments in the same shell mixes up the toolchains.

docs.title: Use the SDK
docs.text:
Source the environment in each new shell:

source $SDK_DIR/environment-setup-aarch64-poky-linux

Check:

echo $CC
echo $CROSS_COMPILE $ARCH
$CC --version

aarch64-poky-linux-gcc -mcpu=cortex-a55 ... --sysroot=/opt/poky/3.1.x/sysroots/aarch64-poky-linux
aarch64-poky-linux- arm64

$CC already contains --sysroot and CPU flags. Always use $CC, never aarch64-poky-linux-gcc alone.

docs.title: Build an application
docs.text:
Single file:

$CC hello.c -o hello
file hello

hello: ELF 64-bit LSB pie executable, ARM aarch64, ...

Makefile project: the SDK exports CC, CXX, CFLAGS, LDFLAGS, so a Makefile that uses these variables works as is:

CFLAGS += -Wall -O2

app: main.o util.o
	$(CC) $(LDFLAGS) $^ -o $@

clean:
	rm -f app *.o

make

Warning

Do not hardcode CC = gcc in the Makefile. It overrides the SDK's cross compiler and builds for the host.

CMake project (requires nativesdk-cmake in the SDK; the environment script then makes cmake use the SDK toolchain file):

cmake -S . -B build
cmake --build build -j$(nproc)

Autotools project:

./configure $CONFIGURE_FLAGS
make -j$(nproc)

docs.title: Copy to the board and run
docs.text:
scp hello root@$BOARD_IP:/home/root/
ssh root@$BOARD_IP /home/root/hello

With NFS boot, copy straight into the exported rootfs instead:

sudo cp hello /nfs/rzg2l/home/root/

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause / fix cannot execute binary file: Exec format error Running an ARM binary on the host, or a host binary on the board. Check with file version 'GLIBC_2.xx' not found on the board SDK built from a different image/BSP than the rootfs. Rebuild the SDK from the running image fatal error: xxx.h: No such file or directory Library's -dev package not in the SDK. Add the library to the image and rebuild the SDK aarch64-poky-linux-ld: unrecognized option '-Wl,-O1' when building the kernel The SDK's LDFLAGS are for gcc, not ld. Run unset LDFLAGS before make in a kernel tree CMake builds for x86 nativesdk-cmake missing from the SDK, or the system cmake was used. Check which cmake
